title: Storage basins
text:
A Basin in a regional model stands for a whole network of waterways. To represent that water does not all flow at once, most Basins come in a pair, with the same area:
Precipitation, evaporation and groundwater reach them differently, see Forcing. In the coupled model, about 9800 of the 20 200 Basins are bergend, and 2300 are hoofdwater, the main water system and the KRW water bodies.
flowchart LR
  subgraph drain["Drains only"]
    b1["bergend"] -->|"TabulatedRatingCurve<br>Van der Gaast"| d1["doorgaand"]
  end
  subgraph both["Can also be supplied"]
    b2["bergend"] <-->|ManningResistance| d2["doorgaand"]
  end


 The two ways in which a storage Basin connects to its doorgaand Basin.

title: Storage basins
text:
Gravity controlled models
pipeline/05_add_bergend.py adds a storage Basin to each Basin with ribasim_nl.berging.VdGaastBerging, from the rasters of the LHM and of Van der Gaast. It drains through a TabulatedRatingCurve.
In the supply areas of verwerkt/sturing/aanvoergebieden.gpkg with meta_aanvoer true, the storage Basin connects with a ManningResistance instead, so it can also be supplied. A Basin counts as supplied if at least half of its area lies in a supply area, see ribasim_nl.berging.supply_area_basin_ids.

title: Storage basins
text:
Level controlled models
The profile generation derives both profiles from the hydro-objects and the BGT, and adds the storage Basins, always with a ManningResistance. Without any usable profile, the Basin keeps one Basin with a fallback profile.

title: Summer and winter levels
text: Many water boards keep a higher target level (streefpeil) in summer than in winter, see issue #893. The models are built with one target level per Basin, meta_streefpeil, from which their control is derived. At the end of their pipeline, the regional models get the summer and winter levels of the peilgebieden of their water board, in ribasim_nl.regional_model.finish_regional_model. koppelen removes them before coupling, since the coupling and its coupling-level check work with the fixed levels, and applies them again to the coupled model at the end.

title: Summer and winter levels
text:
Level management per peilgebied
The peilbeheer stage, pipeline/peilbeheer.py, reads the peilgebieden of the water boards into data/Rijkswaterstaat/verwerkt/peilbeheer.gpkg. For each water board, SOURCES in ribasim_nl.peilbeheer lists the attributes of its dataset per type of level management, as described in the issue. This gives each peilgebied a target level and its lower and upper bound (ondergrens and bovengrens) in summer and winter, and the dates of the transitions between summer and winter. Where the dataset does not give these:

Without a target level, the target level is the mean of the bounds.
A season without a target level gets the levels of the other season, as for a fixed level.
A target level without bounds gets bounds 2.5 cm below and above it, the band of the DiscreteControl thresholds of the model. Bounds on the wrong side of the target level, or more than 0.5 m away from it, are replaced in the same way.
The transition from winter to summer begins on 1 April, and back on 1 October. The end of a transition is 10 days later, if the dataset does not give it.

Levels of 99 m NAP or more are unknown, and so are levels of 0 in the datasets that use 0 for unknown values, those of Hollands Noorderkwartier, Vechtstromen and De Dommel. Peilgebieden of which the summer and winter level differ more than 1 m are left out as data errors, see this list. De Dommel has no peilgebieden, but its weirs have a high and a low target level, WS_STREEFPEILHOOG and WS_STREEFPEILLAAG, which are used as the summer and winter level. Its model already takes the target levels of its Basins from WS_STREEFPEILHOOG. Limburg, Rijn en IJssel, Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard and Vallei en Veluwe have no level management yet.

title: Summer and winter levels
section: Summer and winter in the model
text:
Summer and winter in the model
ribasim_nl.seasonal_levels applies the level management to the Basins with a target level:

A Basin gets the peilgebied of its water board that covers most of it, at least half, or else the weir within 100 m of it with the closest target level. Its target level stays the same in the season of which the target level of the peilgebied is closest to it, since the target levels of the model are checked with the water boards. The peilgebied gives the difference with the other season, and the bounds. If both target levels of the peilgebied are more than 0.5 m from that of the Basin, the peilgebied does not describe its water, and the Basin keeps its fixed level.
Basins that are joined by ManningResistance or LinearResistance nodes are one water in the model, since the flow between them follows their difference in level. So they all get the level management of the largest area of them, also when that is a fixed level, relative to their own target level.
The thresholds of the DiscreteControl conditions on the level of the Basin follow its target level. Thresholds with the default band of 5 cm around a level get the bounds of the target level instead.
The Outlets and Pumps that a DiscreteControl node controls get a winter and a summer variant of each control state, such as afvoer winter and afvoer zomer, with the min_upstream_level and max_downstream_level of that season. An extra condition on the season, on a variable with weight 0, switches between them. It follows the transitions of a Basin around the controlled nodes of which the level changes, preferably one that the DiscreteControl node listens to.
The initial level of the Basin follows its target level at the start of the model.




One Basin in the coupled run, with a median fit to its levels among the Basins with 0.2 to 0.4 m difference. The levels change at once, on 1 April and 1 October, and the Basin mostly stays between its bounds.


The levels change at once, at the begin of each transition. A gradual transition needs Ribasim to support parameters of control states that change over time. The DiscreteControl nodes that change over the year have cyclic timeseries over the first year of the model. The fixed levels and thresholds are kept in the meta_fixed_ columns, from which remove_seasonal_levels restores them. The level management of each Basin is in the meta_ columns of the Basin / area table, with the levels as applied to the model.
Uncontrolled Outlets and Pumps keep their fixed levels, and so do the rating curves of the bergend Basins of the gravity controlled models.

title: Main water system
text:
The model of the main water system holds the rivers, canals and lakes of Rijkswaterstaat. The scripts are in pipeline/rijkswaterstaat, numbered in order of execution, and run in three DVC stages.
flowchart TD
  subgraph frozen["bathymetry, frozen"]
    s1["1_bathymetrie.py<br>verwerkt/bathymetrie"]
  end
  subgraph demand["hws_demand"]
    direction TB
    s2["2_basins.py<br>Basins and profiles"] --> s3["3_netwerk.py<br>verwerkt/netwerk.gpkg"]
    s3 --> s4["4_kunstwerken.py<br>verwerkt/hydamo.gpkg"]
    s4 --> s5["5_model_netwerk.py<br>modellen/hws_netwerk"]
    s5 --> s6["6_model_sturing.py<br>modellen/hws_sturing"]
    s6 --> s7["7_model_onttrekkingen.py<br>modellen/hws_demand"]
    s7 --> s8a["8a_update_state.py<br>modellen/hws_demand"]
  end

  end

title: Main water system
text:
Bathymetry
1_bathymetrie.py merges data from Baseline (version j23_6-v1, non-public) with grids from bathymetrie-Nederland into one 5 × 5 m GeoTIFF. Both are needed, since the Midden Limburgse en Noord Brabantse kanalen are not in Baseline, and the IJsselmeer is not completely covered in bathymetrie-Nederland. For the mask we use Top10NL waterdelen and manually filled a boolean column baseline.
This stage is frozen, so it is not run again in a reproduction, since the source data does not change.






Bathymetry mask







Bathymetry

title: Main water system
text:
From data to a network

2_basins.py derives the Basin areas of the main water system. From the bathymetry it writes a CSV file with the profile of each Basin, verwerkt/basins_level_area.csv.
3_netwerk.py derives a ribasim_nl.Network (not a Ribasim network yet!) from OpenStreetMap, with modifications mainly in the IJsselmeer, to build the model network with in 5_model_netwerk.py. It needs the Basins of 2_basins.py, since a network node goes at each intersection of a Basin area with the network. This network, verwerkt/netwerk.gpkg, also guides the links in the coupling.
4_kunstwerken.py combines the structures from NIS (Netwerk Informatie Systeem) of Rijkswaterstaat, Baseline, OpenStreetMap, the structures in the primary flood defences, and the abstractions, into a HyDAMO-based format, from which the Ribasim network is derived.
5_model_netwerk.py combines the results of steps 2 to 4 into a first Ribasim model, modellen/hws_netwerk/hws.toml. It includes the distribution keys (verdeelsleutels) of Lobith and Monsin as structures, but no control nodes, and no demands.

title: Main water system
text:
Control and demands

6_model_sturing.py adds control, with ContinuousControl, DiscreteControl and FlowDemand nodes, into modellen/hws_sturing/hws.toml.
7_model_onttrekkingen.py adds the demands of drinking water, industry and energy as UserDemands, splits Basins along a route where needed, and adds Junctions, into modellen/hws_demand/hws.toml.
8a_update_state.py runs this model, and writes its final state back as its initial state.

title: Main water system
text:
Boundaries and forcing
8b_update_bc.py makes the model that goes into the coupling, modellen/hws_transient, for 2017 up to 2020:



What
Source




Discharges of the Rhine at Lobith and the Meuse at Monsin
Daily means, aangeleverd/Matroos_debieten_2017_2022_Lobith_Monsin.xlsx


Levels at Kornwerderzand and Den Oever
A seasonal table of −0.4 to −0.1 m, repeated every year


Level at IJmuiden
Constant −0.4 m


Precipitation and evaporation
LHM, as in the forcing of the regional models


Wastewater
The RWZI model


Measurements
Observation nodes, see ribasim_nl.observations



The other model in this folder that is tracked, hws_2025_10_1, is a fixed earlier version, from which the fix script of Vechtstromen reads the polygon of the Twentekanaal.

title: Level controlled
text:
The level controlled (peilbeheerst) models cover 10 water authorities: Amstel, Gooi en Vecht, Delfland, Hollands Noorderkwartier, Hollandse Delta, Rijnland, Rivierenland, Scheldestromen, Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard, Wetterskip Fryslân and Zuiderzeeland. These authorities keep target levels in many small level areas (peilgebieden), so their model follows the areas and the structures between them. HKV made their first input models in 2024 and 2025, and the pipeline now makes these from the data the water authorities delivered, in aangeleverd.
flowchart LR
  subgraph input["Input model"]
    direction TB
    a["00_postprocess.py<br>verwerkt/postprocessed.gpkg"] --> b["00c_parse_crossings.py<br>verwerkt/crossings.gpkg"]
    b --> c["00d_shortest_paths.py<br>verwerkt/shortest_path.gpkg"]
    c --> d["00e_crossings_to_ribasim.py<br>_boezemmodel_<version>"]
  end
  subgraph model["Regional model"]
    direction TB
    e["01_feedback.py<br>_feedback"] --> f["02_profiles.py<br>_profiles"]
    f --> g["03_forcing.py<br>_forcing"]
  end
  input --> model --> merge["samenvoegen"]


 The stages of a level controlled model, with the result of each.
The maps below show the same 5 × 5 km of Delfland near Delft, at each step.

title: Level controlled
text:
The input model
The code is in ribasim_nl.crossings.


1. The delivery
pipeline/<water board>/00_postprocess.py makes the postprocessed data, verwerkt/postprocessed.gpkg: the peilgebieden with their streefpeilen and aggregation areas, the hydro-objects, culverts, stuwen and gemalen. Where HKV corrected the delivered data by hand, it applies these corrections, verwerkt/corrections.gpkg.





The postprocessed data. Grey lines are the hydro-objects, with stuwen in orange and gemalen in black. Thin lines are the boundaries of the peilgebieden, and the boezem is blue.






2. Crossings and shortest paths
pipeline/00c_parse_crossings.py finds the crossings of the hydro-objects with the boundaries of the peilgebieden, with the stuwen and gemalen at them, and writes them to verwerkt/crossings.gpkg.
pipeline/00d_shortest_paths.py finds the shortest paths along the hydro-objects through each boezem, from each of its crossings to its centre, and writes them to verwerkt/shortest_path.gpkg.





The crossings with a structure in black, and those without in grey. Blue lines are the shortest paths through the boezems.






3. The input model
pipeline/00e_crossings_to_ribasim.py makes the input model modellen/<water board>_boezemmodel_<version>: the aggregation areas become Basins, and the crossings connector nodes. It numbers the nodes and links after the input model of 2024, verwerkt/boezemmodel_ids.gpkg, to which the feedback forms and scripts refer, by matching the nodes by type and location, see ribasim_nl.crossings.renumber.





The input model. Each aggregation area is one Basin, in its own colour, with straight links to the structures on its boundary.




This code is a port of the code that made the input models in 2024 and 2025, see Reproducing models. Since the nodes are numbered after the input models of 2024, the deliveries, the aggregation areas and the algorithms can change, while the feedback forms keep referring to the right nodes, as long as these can be matched. The corrections refer to the delivered rows by their code, and apply_edits stops at corrections of rows that a new delivery lacks, so check them when the delivery changes.

title: Level controlled
text:
The regional model
The DVC pipeline then builds the model of each water board with three stages:

feedback_<water board> runs pipeline/<water board>/01_feedback.py, which applies the feedback form of the water board with RibasimFeedbackProcessor, followed by edits by hand. In 5 water boards it finally splits large Basins.
profiles_<water board> runs pipeline/prep_cross_sections.py and pipeline/<water board>/02_profiles.py, the profile generation, which gives each Basin a profile and adds its storage basin.
forcing_<water board> runs pipeline/<water board>/03_forcing.py, with the steps below.






flowchart TD
  a["set_boundary_conditions<br>forcing, boundary levels"] --> b["set_aanvoer_flags<br>which Basins can be supplied"]
  b --> c["categorize_nodes<br>which nodes supply and drain"]
  c --> d["add_controllers<br>control per function"]
  d --> e["complete_parametrization<br>authorities, inflows, known capacities"]
  e --> f["set_design_capacities<br>capacity from the drained area"]
  f --> g["write_and_run_forcing_model<br>layout, levels, write, run, check"]


 The steps of a typical forcing script, mostly in ribasim_nl.workflow. 



The steps the forcing scripts have in common are in ribasim_nl.workflow. See control, forcing, design capacities and layout. The forcing, the foreign inflows and RWZIs, and the final steps that lay out, write and run the model are shared with the gravity controlled models, see ribasim_nl.regional_model. Unlike those, the forcing stage also runs and checks a dry and a wet steady state model, see Testing.



The final model of the same area, Delfland_forcing. Basins come in pairs of a through-flow and a storage Basin, and the links follow the watercourses, with Junctions where they join.

title: Model derivation
text:
Where the data is
Everything is under data, with a folder per authority, named as in ribasim_nl.aquo, and Basisgegevens for national data:







Folder
Content




<authority>/aangeleverd
Data as delivered by the authority


<authority>/verwerkt
Processed data, including hand-made edits such as model_edits.gpkg


<authority>/modellen
The models of each stage, such as <authority>_dynamic_model


Rijkswaterstaat/modellen
Also the merged lhm_parts and coupled lhm_coupled models


Rijkswaterstaat/runs/lhm_coupled
The latest run of the coupled model, with its results



Get data explains how to download these.

title: Model derivation
text:
Node IDs
Scripts and edit files refer to nodes by their ID, in the model of the authority. Merging keeps these unique by prefixing them with the waterbeheercode of the authority, see ribasim_nl.aquo:
\[\text{node ID in the coupled model} = \text{waterbeheercode} \times 100\,000 + \text{node ID in the regional model}\]
So 203892 is node 3892 of Wetterskip Fryslân, with code 2, and 8009406 is node 9406 of Rijkswaterstaat, with code 80. The model viewer shows the same IDs. Fix a problem in the stages of the authority where possible, rather than in the coupling, so that the regional model and the nationwide model stay alike.
The IDs must stay the same on every run, or all these references break, see Reproducing models.

title: Forcing
text:
The regional models and the main water system share their forcing, in ribasim_nl.regional_model, for 2017 up to 2020. The run of the coupled model covers the first 2 of these 3 years.
flowchart LR
  lhm["LHM 4.3 results<br>LHM_433_budgets_update_makkink"] --> meteo["Precipitation,<br>evaporation"]
  lhm --> budgets["Drainage, infiltration,<br>surface runoff, sprinkling"]
  meteo --> basin["Basin / time"]
  budgets --> basin
  foreign["Measured foreign inflows<br>BuitenlandseAanvoer"] --> flow["FlowBoundary / time"]
  rwzi["RWZI model<br>Z-info, RwziBase"] --> flow
  flow --> model["Regional model"]
  basin --> model
  model --> fractions["LHM fractions<br>for tracing water"]

title: Forcing
text:
Precipitation and evaporation
Both come from the results of LHM 4.3, averaged per Basin, see ribasim_nl.set_forcing. Evaporation is the Makkink reference evaporation times the open water factor of Mozart, by month and decade. An LHM day starts at 09:00 in model time, so the forcing starts on the day before the start of the model.

title: Forcing
text:
Drainage, infiltration and runoff
ribasim_nl.assign_offline_budgets adds the MODFLOW-MetaSWAP budgets of the LHM, summed per Basin: negative values become drainage, and positive values infiltration.







Budget
Goes to




bdgriv_sys1, 4, 5
doorgaand and hoofdwater Basins


bdgriv_sys2, 3, 6, bdgdrn_sys1, 2, 3
bergend Basins


bdgqrun
surface_runoff


bdgpssw, sprinkling
hoofdwater and doorgaand Basins in the gravity controlled models, bergend Basins in the level controlled models



The script writes the budgets to mfms_budgets.arrow, and a check of the assignment to results/assign_validation.png in the model folder.

title: Forcing
text:
Foreign inflows
Streams from Germany and Belgium enter as FlowBoundaries with meta_categorie “buitenlandse aanvoer”. src/ribasim_nl/ribasim_nl/data/buitenlandse_aanvoer.csv lists the 55 inflows, all in Brabantse Delta, De Dommel, Limburg, Rijn en IJssel and Vechtstromen. ribasim_nl.transboundary_inflow matches them to the boundaries by name and location, and sets measured daily values from Basisgegevens/BuitenlandseAanvoer, with gaps interpolated. Outside the measurements, or without any, the inflow is the constant in that table.

title: Forcing
text:
Wastewater
The stage rwzi makes a separate model with pipeline/create_rwzi_model.py, of one FlowBoundary per treatment plant, linked to a Terminal at its discharge point. The flow rates are daily influent from Z-info, or else the yearly values of RwziBase, spread evenly over the days.





flowchart LR
  a["RWZI FlowBoundary"] --> b["Junction, was the Terminal"]
  b --> c["Route into or<br>out of the Basin"]






merge_rwzi_model adds the plants that discharge in the model, within 100 m of a Basin that is not bergend, or 3000 m in the main water system, and removes the others. attach_rwzi_junctions then moves each Junction onto the nearest route into or out of its Basin.

title: Forcing
text:
Fractions
ribasim_nl.assign_lhm_fractions labels the water by its origin, such as precipitation, drainage, or the neighbouring authority. The model then tracks these fractions through the network, and ribasim_nl.delwaq can use them for water quality with Delwaq.

title: Coupling
text:
The nationwide model is made in two stages. samenvoegen merges the 22 models into one model file in which they are still separate, lhm_parts. koppelen connects them where they meet, into lhm_coupled.
flowchart LR
  hws["hws_transient"] --> merge
  gravity["11 <authority>_dynamic_model"] --> merge
  level["10 <authority>_forcing"] --> merge
  merge(["samenvoegen<br>08_samenvoegen_modellen.py"]) --> parts["lhm_parts"]
  parts --> couple(["koppelen<br>09_koppelen_modellen.py"])
  netwerk["netwerk.gpkg, Top10NL"] --> couple
  peilbeheer["peilbeheer.gpkg"] --> couple
  couple --> coupled["lhm_coupled"]

  classDef step fill:#dfedef,stroke:#0c6a77
  class merge,couple step

title: Coupling
text:
Merging
pipeline/08_samenvoegen_modellen.py reads each model, makes its IDs unique with prefix_index, see Node IDs, and appends all its tables with concat. The original IDs stay available in meta_node_id_waterbeheerder and meta_link_id_waterbeheerder, and meta_waterbeheerder holds the authority. The merged model starts with the settings of the model of the main water system, and the solver settings are set here.

title: Coupling
text:
Connecting the models
In each regional model, a LevelBoundary stands for the water on the other side of its border. AssignAuthorities records whose water that is in the column meta_couple_authority of the node table, with Noordzee or Buitenland where it leaves the model. The boundaries of the main water system have none, so they stay boundaries.
process_boundary_nodes then goes through the boundaries of the regional models:





flowchart TD
  start["LevelBoundary"] --> own{"Couples to its own authority,<br>Noordzee or Buitenland?"}
  own -->|yes| stays["Stays a boundary"]
  own -->|no| forced{"In forced_coupling?"}
  forced -->|yes| target["Connect to the given<br>Basin or Junction"]
  forced -->|no| near{"Boundaries of the other authority<br>within 20 m?"}
  near -->|"more than one"| stays
  near -->|one| pair{"Two Outlets in opposite directions,<br>both with or both without control?"}
  pair -->|yes| merged["Merge into one Outlet"]
  pair -->|no| basin
  near -->|none| basin["Connect to the nearest Basin / area<br>of the other authority"]


 What happens to a LevelBoundary with a meta_couple_authority. 



Connecting to the nearest Basin is the easiest and most common case. It relinks the connector nodes of the boundary, for instance an Outlet, so an inflow into the boundary becomes an outlet into the Basin, and an outflow becomes an inlet from it. If a path in the opposite direction already exists, that path and the connector are removed instead, to avoid a cycle. replace_listen_node_id points control nodes that listened to the boundary to the node that replaces it. For the Basins of Rijkswaterstaat, the new link follows the topology of Rijkswaterstaat/verwerkt/netwerk.gpkg, instead of a direct line. No new control nodes are added.
Two LevelBoundaries close to one another, especially between two water boards, are treated as duplicates, and merged if they meet the conditions above.
Where two Pumps, or an Outlet and a Pump, meet at a border, or Outlets do not meet these conditions, they are handled as a connector to a Basin. That leaves duplicate connector nodes in place, and might duplicate a flow. Still to do are couplings for Pump | LevelBoundary . LevelBoundary | Pump and Pump | LevelBoundary . LevelBoundary | Outlet, and investigating whether other connections happen.






Before coupling, in lhm_parts. Rijnland (green) and Amstel, Gooi en Vecht (blue) both end in LevelBoundaries (triangles) along their border.







After coupling, in lhm_coupled. Each pair of LevelBoundaries with the Outlets next to it is now one Outlet (square) with links to both sides.





forced_coupling lists the exceptions, usually with an issue that explains them. For instance, LevelBoundary 1500551 of Delfland couples to Basin 4000298, the Brielse Meer, rather than to the nearest Basin in the Hartelkanaal.

title: Coupling
text:
The other steps of koppelen
couple_model in pipeline/09_koppelen_modellen.py runs these steps in order:

Remove the summer and winter levels, since the coupling and its level check work with fixed levels, and the nodes listed in remove_nodes, mostly structures that belong to the neighbouring model and boundaries without a link.
Replace the boundaries, as above.
Set names and levels of the nodes where a boundary was a placeholder.
Convert open connections: convert_outlets_to_manning_resistance turns Outlets on open water, such as 1100600 Angstel-ARK (#820), into ManningResistances.
Fix profiles: where an Outlet has a min_upstream_level below the bottom of the Basin upstream of it, the bottom of the Basin moves down.
Remove invalid nodes, with a warning: remove_invalid_topology_nodes removes nodes that the coupling left without a valid topology.
Route the links between models over Top10NL, with netwerk.gpkg as the main route. A link stays straight if it is listed in straight_rws_links, such as those of the Zeesluis Muiden (#916).
Add user demands that cross models, such as the Evides drinking water of the Maasvlakte (#857).
Attach RWZIs to the routes of Basins that only exist after coupling. For instance, RWZI Stein discharges to the Julianakanaal instead of a Basin of Limburg.
Link observations that measure on links between models, which need the coupled network, see ribasim_nl.observations.
Tidy the layout, see Layout.
Write the model, validate it with validate_ribasim_nl, and write the links that were added to link.gpkg.
Correct the coupling levels, see below.
Apply the summer and winter levels again, without changing the initial state, since the final state of the regional models already follows the seasons.

title: Vallei en Veluwe
text:
Eemland
De polders in het noorden van het gebied worden van water voorzien vanuit de Eem. Deze staat in open verbinding met de Randmeren (Eemmeer). Het peil van de randmeren is van invloed op de uitlaatcapaciteit. De belangrijkste inlaten zijn gemaal Maatpolder, Sluis de Laak, inlaatduiker Arkersluis en Gemaal Hertogh Reijnnout. Water wordt via poldergemalen aan onder andere de Eem verder over gebied verspreid.

title: Vallei en Veluwe
text:
Gelderse Vallei
Inlaat Grebbesluis laat in de zomer water in via de Nederrijn naar het Valleikanaal voor doorspoeling ten behoeve van de waterkwaliteit.

title: Vallei en Veluwe
text:
Noordwest Veluwe
Aanvoergebied Noordwest Veluwe wordt in droge periode door gemaal De Wenden Oosterwolde van water voorzien. Ook liggen er inlaten aan het Veluwemeer en Drontermeer die onder vrij verval water inlaten in droge perioden.

title: Vallei en Veluwe
text:
IJsselvallei
Via gemaal mr. A.C. Baron van der Feltz (Terwolde) wordt aanvoergebied de IJsselvallei voorzien van water in droge perioden. Via diverse inlaten en poldergemalen wordt het water over het aanvoergebied verdeeld.

Een groot deel van het Apeldoornsch kanaal wordt door kwel uit het grondwater gevoed. in extreem droge tijden kan via inlaat Dieren water van de IJssel in het Apeldoornsch kanaal worden geleid.

title: Rijn en IJssel
text:
Laatst bijgewerkt: 27-4-2026
Bekijk het model in de modelviewer






Systeembeschrijving Rijn en IJssel




Water wordt aangevoerd naar een aantal beken vanuit het Twentekanaal in het noorden van het beheergebied. Daarnaast vindt aanvoer plaats vanuit Duitsland. Dit water wordt op meerdere locaties verdeeld en lokaal ingelaten.
De afvoer vindt plaats via de Twentekanalen, de IJssel en de Rijn.
Hieronder worden de belangrijkste systemen beknopt beschreven. De focus ligt hierbij op belangrijke verdeelwerken en aanvoer-condities.




De Schipbeek ontvangt daarnaast water vanuit Duitsland via de Buurserbeek en Zoddebeek. Bovenstrooms van het Twentekanaal wordt via de Schipbeek een deel van het water doorgevoerd naar Vechtstromen (Boven-Regge, niet op de kaart). Bij het Twentekanaal kan water worden ingelaten via Inlaat Schipbeek, waar maximaal 1.4 m3/s wordt ingelaten. De Schipbeek voert af op de IJssel en via een noodoverloop op het Twentekanaal (max 8 m3/s).



De Eefse Beek voert af via het Twentekanaal via een uitlaatwerk, onder vrij verval, of via Gemaal Oude Eefsebeek. Via Inlaat Herkel kan maximaal 0.6 m3/s worden aangevoerd vanuit het Twentekanaal.



De Baakse Beek en Veengoot ontspringen in Nederland. Bij Verdeelwerk Hackfort wordt 0.1-0.3 m3/s doorgelaten richting de Baakse Beek en de rest afgevoerd via het Stroomkanaal van Hackfort. Bij hoog water op de IJssel kan water ook worden uitgemalen via gemaal Baakse Beek.



De Berkel ontvangt water uit Duitsland. Dit wordt verdeelt bij verdeelwerk Haarlo; 40-45% gaat richting de Bolksbeek en 55-60% richting de Berkel. In aanvoersituaties kan het water uit de Bolksbeek lokaal worden ingelaten. Het restant watert af op het Twentekanaal.
Langs de Berkel, bedenstrooms Haarlo zijn twee verdeelwerken, Honebrug en Beekvliet, waar bovenstrooms ook water kan worden ingelaten. Beekvliet is ook het punt waar de Slinge in de Berkel stroomt.
Bij Verdeelwerk Lochem wordt, wanneer beschikbaar, 3m/s doorgelaten over de Berkel richting Zutphen. Bij hogere afvoeren wordt tot 32 m3/s afgevoerd via het Twenteknaal via het aflaatwerk. Bij hogere afvoeren gaat de rest over de Berkel richting Warken. Tussen Verdeelwerk Lochem en Warken wordt ook water ingelaten bij Inlaat Lochem.
Bij Warken wordt 0.9 m3/s doorgelaten via de Berkel. Ook wordt hier 0.1 m3/s doorgelaten richting de Brummeler Laak. Dit wordt uitgemalen bij gemaal Helbergen



De bovenlopen van de Oude-IJssel ontvangen water vanuit Duitsland; 70% van het totale oppervlak van het stroomgebied ligt in Duitsland. Bij Verdeelwerk Bredevoort watert de Schaarsbeek af op de Keizersbeek via een sifon. Hier kan overtollig water uit de Schaarsbeek worden afgelaten richting de Boven-Slinge. Ook kan water uit de Boven-Slinge worden ingelaten op de Kiezersbeek.
Afvoer van de Oude-IJssel vindt plaats naar de IJssel bij sluis-stuwcomplex Doesburg. Gemaal Doesburg zorgt voor extra capaciteit met 1 m3/s.




Per kunstwerk, gespecificeerd op naam, code (waterbeheerder), node_id (v.h. Ribasim model) zijn hieronder de functie (inlaat, doorlaat, uitlaat, uitlaat (doorspoeling))) en de capaciteiten onder aanvoer en afvoer condities opgegeven.

Systeembeschrijving Limburg


Hieronder is de sturing van de aanvoergebieden beschreven uit bovenstaande figuur.


Via gemaal Katsberg wordt water (max 5.4m3/s) vanuit de Noordervaart aangevoerd naar het kanaal van Deurne.Water wordt ingelaten voor WPM en Aa en Maas in de verdeling 50-50%.
Bij Verdeelwerk de Halte wordt het beschikbare water verdeeld over het Peelkanaal en de Grenssloot verdeeld. Middels een automatische klepstuw (Gre 6 en TMX De Halte), wordt hier het aanvoerwater van de Katsberg doorgezet naar de Grenssloot. Deze stuw is zowel peil als debiet gestuurd Het peil mag nooit lager dan 30.80 vanwege inklappen veenwanden en nooit hoger dan 31.21 vanwege overstromingsgevaar bovenstrooms.
In de zomer wordt gestuurd op een peil van 31.12m+NAP. In de winter sturing op 31.19m+NAP (om de veenkades zo nat mogelijk te houden ter voorkoming van inklinking). Het debiet is de resultante van de optelsom vanaf Katsberg en klopt in de zomer vrij goed.
De Helenavaart takt aan op Kanaal van Deurne via stuw Hel 1 (automatische stuw). Overtollig water van Helenavaart wordt naar Peelkanaal geleid.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text: Hieronder is de sturing van de aanvoergebieden beschreven uit bovenstaande figuur.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Boezem Noordwest
Het gebied Boezem Noordwest wordt van water voorzien door de inlaat bij gemaal Stroink.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Drentse Hoofdvaart
Via de Paradijssluis wordt water ingelaten vanuit het Meppelerdiep naar de Drentsche Hoofdvaart. De Drentsche Hoofdvaart loopt van het Meppelerdiep tot aan het Noord-Willemskanaal. De Drentsche Hoofdvaart is verdeeld in zes panden. Deze panden worden gescheiden door sluizen. Tussen de panden vindt water transport plaats via sluizen en pompen. De sluizen zijn gezien van de Paradijssluis naar het Noord-Willemskanaal; de Paradijssluis, de Haveltersluis, de Uffeltersluis, de Dieversluis, de Haarsluis en de Veenesluis. Het pand benedenstrooms van Haarsluis staat in open verbinding met de Beilervaart waarna het bij aanvoergemaal de Holthe verder naar de Hoogeveensche Vaart kan worden aangevoerd indien daar tekorten zijn.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Wold Aa
Via de Wold Aa wordt water via aanvoergemaal Blijdenstein ingelaten waarna het via verschillende aanvoergemalen verder wordt opgemalen, met als laatste aanvoergemaal Oldenhave

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Hoogeveensche Vaart
Via de Rogatsluis wordt water ingelaten vanuit het Meppelerdiep naar de Hoogeveensche Vaart. De Hoogeveensche Vaart bestaat uit vier panden. Deze panden zijn gescheiden door sluizen. Dit zijn gezien van de Verlengde Hoogeveensche Vaart naar het Meppelerdiep; de Noordscheschutsluis, de Nieuwebrugsluis, de Ossesluis en de Rogatsluis. In het oosten van aanvoergebied Hoogeveensche Vaart liggen diverse doorlaten vanuit Vechtstromen.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Ankersmit
Via aanvoergemaal Ankersmit wordt water via de IJssel aangevoerd naar het Overijssels Kanaal. In werkelijkheid komt dit water niet verder dan een dam ten noorden van Raalte.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Overijssels Kanaal
Aanvoergebied Overijssels Kanaal wordt aangevoerd vanuit het Overijssels Kanaal via Hancate (Vechtstromen).

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Westerveld
Via inlaat Westerveld wordt water aangevoerd vanuit het Zwarte Water naar de Soestwetering.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Dedemsvaart
Via het Galgenrak wordt water ingelaten naar de Demdemsvaart. Aan de Demdesvaart liggen diverse inlaten om het aangevoerde water over het aanvoergebied te verdelen.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
Vecht-Twentekanalen
Via het Ommerkanaal wordt het water ingelaten bij Langewijk Emsland1 en 2 in het aanvoergebied Vecht-Twentekanalen. Verder zitten er nog divese inlaten aan de Overrijselse Vecht die dit gebied van water voorzien.

title: Drents Overijsselse Delta
text:
IJsselmeergebied
Het IJsselmeergebied wordt van water voorzien door diverse inlaten aan de IJssel, het Zwartemeer/Zwarte Water en het Meppelerdiep.

Systeembeschrijving Brabantse Delta


Hieronder is de sturing van het Mark-Vliet systeem en de aanvoergebieden beschreven uit bovenstaande figuur.


De Mark, Dintel, Mark-Vlietkanaal, de Roosendaalsche en Steenbergsche Vliet en het Markkanaal staan in open verbinding met elkaar. Bij droogte vindt aanvoer in eerste instantie plaats vanuit het Volkerak. Wanneer dit niet genoeg is kan via de Markduiker water aangevoerd worden.



De Marksluis kent in principe alleen schutverliezen. Bij een hoger waterpeil op de Mark dan op de Amertak kunnen de extra deuren worden gesloten om instroom van hoogwater richting het kanaal te voorkomen. De sluis fungeert dan tevens als waterkering.



Afvoer: - Via de Slagen pomp en gemaal Keizersveer wordt het water afgevoerd naar de Bergsche Maas - In noordoosten watert een klein gebied Gansoijen (noordoosten) via een sifon onder het Afwateringskanaal ’s-Hertogenosch-Drongelen door via het (Aa en Maas) afgevoerd naar de Bergsche Maas. Bij Waalwijk watert nog een klein gebied via gemaal Bloemendaal op het Drongelenskanaal (mondt uit in de Bergsche Maas). - Ten zuiden van het Wilhelminakanaal watert het via aflaatkunstwerk af op het Wilhelminakanaal. Het overige deel van het water wordt via een sifon (Tichelrijt) onder het Wilhelminakanaal geleid en watert af via gemaal Keizersveer op de Bergsche Maas.
Aanvoer: - Vanuit het Wilhelminakanaal zijn diverse inlaten die de Donge, en Paterheide van aanvoer voorzien. - Aanvoergebied de Sprangsloot ontvangt water via inlaat de Sprangse sloot vanuit het Zuiderkanaal die in de zomer op peil wordt gehouden door de Bergsche Maas ????? - De Westplas ontvangt direct water uit de Bergsche Maas



Afvoer: - Vindt plaats vanaf de Mark, via M-V sluis naar het Volkerak - Rechtstreeks naar de Amer en via de Amertak naar de Amer
Aanvoer - De aanvoer vindt plaats via inlaten via de Mark



Afvoer: - Vindt plaats vanaf de Mark, via M-V sluis naar het Volkerak - Rechtstreeks en via de Roode Vaartnaar het Hollandsch diep
Aanvoer - De aanvoer vindt plaats via inlaten via de Mark die op peil wordt gehouden door het Volkerak??



Afvoer: - Vindt plaats vanaf de Mark-Vlietkanaal en de Dintel , via M-V sluis naar het Volkerak - Vanaf de Steenbergsche Vliet via de scheepvaartsluis naar de Krammer
Aanvoer - De aanvoer vindt plaats via inlaten vanaf de Dintel en de Steenbergsche Vliet



Afvoer: - Vindt plaats vanaf de Steenbergsche Vliet via de scheepvaartsluis naar de Krammer
Aanvoer: - Vindt plaats vanaf de Steenbergsche Vliet.



Afvoer: - Vindt plaats via een gemaal direct op het Schelde Rijn-kanaal
Aanvoer: - Vindt plaats via een inlaat vanaf het Zoommeer.



Afvoer: - Vindt plaats vanaf de Mark, via M-V sluis naar het Volkerak
Aanvoer: - De aanvoer vindt plaats via inlaten via de Mark/Markkanaal die op peil wordt gehouden door het Volkerak??

title: webmap_publish
text:
webmap_publish
Publish the export_webmap output to MinIO for the model viewer on the documentation site.
pixi run publish-webmap            # the model of the pull request of this branch, compared with its base
pixi run publish-webmap --pr 123   # the model of the working tree as that pull request
pixi run publish-webmap --main     # only the model of origin/main
pixi run publish-webmap --commit REV [--base REV]  # the model of a commit, compared with another commit
Everything is uploaded below the anonymously readable doc-image/webmap/ prefix:

files/<hash>.<ext>: the exported files, named by their content hash, so files that did not change are uploaded once and shared by all models.
lhm_coupled/snapshots/<md5>/manifest.json: the manifest of an export, with the paths of the files in files/. The snapshot is named by the DVC hash of the export_webmap output in dvc.lock, which is how the viewer finds the model of main: it reads dvc.lock from GitHub.
lhm_coupled/main.json: the snapshot of the latest published main, for when the snapshot of the current main is not published.
lhm_coupled/diffs/<base md5>-<head md5>.json: the differences between two snapshots, see ribasim_nl.webmap_diff.
lhm_coupled/prs/<number>.json: the snapshots and differences of a pull request, which the viewer shows for ?pr=<number>. A pull request is compared with main, or in a stack of pull requests with the pull request of its base branch, so it only shows its own changes. That pull request must be published first.

The viewer finds the model of any commit on GitHub, for ?commit=<commit>, by the snapshot in its dvc.lock, and compares it with that of another commit, for ?base=<commit>&commit=<commit>, if their differences are published. It pins the link to the latest main to its commit, so a copied link keeps showing the same model.
DVC does not cache the export_webmap output, so this is the only copy that is kept. The export of another commit, to compare with, is downloaded from its published snapshot. If it is not published, the model is exported again from its run, which DVC does keep.
This needs the following environment variables to be set in .env (Deltares only): AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY They need to have write permission. A pull request is found and commented on with the GitHub CLI gh.

title: webmap
text:
webmap
Export a Ribasim model to web-friendly files for the documentation model viewer.





Name
Description




attribute_tables
List the non-spatial Ribasim tables in a GeoPackage.


color_domain
Robust color scale domain: 2nd to 98th percentile, of magnitudes for log and diverging scales.


downcast_int64
Cast int64 columns that fit to int32, since JavaScript readers return int64 as BigInt.


export_basin_area
Export Basin / area polygons as vector tiles; attributes are looked up by node_id.


export_control
Export the control state changes per DiscreteControl node, sorted by control_node_id and time.


export_gpkg_table
Export a GeoPackage attribute table sorted by node_id, return the number of rows.


export_links
Export the Link table with simplified geometry as interleaved lon/lat coords, sorted by link_id.


export_netcdf_table
Export a (time, node_id) NetCDF input table to long-format float32 Parquet sorted by node_id.


export_nodes
Export the Node table with all attributes and lon/lat columns, sorted by node_id.


export_observations
Export how well the results fit the measurements of the Observation nodes, see ribasim_nl.goodness_of_fit.


export_results
Export Basin and flow results, both per feature for charts and per time step for the map.


export_waterboards
Export simplified water board boundaries as GeoJSON.


export_webmap
Export a Ribasim model to a directory of web-friendly files plus a manifest.json.


file_hash
Return a short content hash of a file, used for cache busting.


flat_coords
Return per-LineString interleaved float32 lon/lat coordinate arrays.


float32_column_paths
The Parquet column path of each float32 column by name, also of float32 lists like the link coords.


float_encoding
Parquet writer options that store float columns with byte stream split, which compresses well.


lonlat_columns
Add float32 x (longitude) and y (latitude) columns from point geometries.


model_input_dir
The input directory of a model, with its database.gpkg.


model_results_dir
The results directory of a model, which may not exist.


netcdf_tables
Map table names like “Basin / time” to the NetCDF files referenced in the TOML.


observed_variable_attrs
The attributes of the simulated values of an observed variable: the flow rate of links, or a Basin variable.


read_config
Read a Ribasim TOML, return the config, the input directory and the database path.


read_features
Read a layer whose id column is the GeoPackage FID, so GDAL does not return it as a column.


read_netcdf
Read the (time, id) variables of a Ribasim NetCDF file as float32 (id, time) arrays sorted by id.


run_info
When the model was run, from ribasim.log, and from which commits, from runinfo.json next to the TOML.


table_slug
Convert a Ribasim table name like “Basin / profile” to “basin_profile”.


write_by_id
Write long-format Parquet sorted by id, one row group per block of ids, for per-feature time series.


write_by_time
Write Parquet ordered by time then id, one row group per block of time steps, for map animation.


write_parquet
Write a DataFrame to Parquet, see write_table.


write_table
Write zstd compressed Parquet with column statistics for row group lookup.





webmap.attribute_tables(database)
List the non-spatial Ribasim tables in a GeoPackage.



webmap.color_domain(values, scale)
Robust color scale domain: 2nd to 98th percentile, of magnitudes for log and diverging scales.



webmap.downcast_int64(table)
Cast int64 columns that fit to int32, since JavaScript readers return int64 as BigInt.



webmap.export_basin_area(database, path)
Export Basin / area polygons as vector tiles; attributes are looked up by node_id.



webmap.export_control(source, path)
Export the control state changes per DiscreteControl node, sorted by control_node_id and time.



webmap.export_gpkg_table(database, name, path)
Export a GeoPackage attribute table sorted by node_id, return the number of rows.



webmap.export_links(database, path)
Export the Link table with simplified geometry as interleaved lon/lat coords, sorted by link_id.



webmap.export_netcdf_table(source, path)
Export a (time, node_id) NetCDF input table to long-format float32 Parquet sorted by node_id.



webmap.export_nodes(database, path)
Export the Node table with all attributes and lon/lat columns, sorted by node_id.



webmap.export_observations(database, results_dir, times, output_dir)
Export how well the results fit the measurements of the Observation nodes, see ribasim_nl.goodness_of_fit.
The fit of each observed variable over the whole run is written as a table, and the difference simulated - observed at each of the times for the map, which is NaN where either value is missing. Returns None if no Observation node is compared.



webmap.export_results(results_dir, output_dir)
Export Basin and flow results, both per feature for charts and per time step for the map.



webmap.export_waterboards(source, path)
Export simplified water board boundaries as GeoJSON.



webmap.export_webmap(toml_path, waterboards_path, output_dir)
Export a Ribasim model to a directory of web-friendly files plus a manifest.json.
The water boards are left out if waterboards_path is None. The viewer fetches files as <path>?v=<hash> so they can be cached indefinitely.



webmap.file_hash(path)
Return a short content hash of a file, used for cache busting.



webmap.flat_coords(geometry)
Return per-LineString interleaved float32 lon/lat coordinate arrays.



webmap.float32_column_paths(schema)
The Parquet column path of each float32 column by name, also of float32 lists like the link coords.



webmap.float_encoding(*dictionary_columns, data)
Parquet writer options that store float columns with byte stream split, which compresses well.



webmap.lonlat_columns(gdf)
Add float32 x (longitude) and y (latitude) columns from point geometries.



webmap.model_input_dir(toml_path, config)
The input directory of a model, with its database.gpkg.



webmap.model_results_dir(toml_path, config)
The results directory of a model, which may not exist.



webmap.netcdf_tables(config, input_dir)
Map table names like “Basin / time” to the NetCDF files referenced in the TOML.



webmap.observed_variable_attrs(results_dir, variable)
The attributes of the simulated values of an observed variable: the flow rate of links, or a Basin variable.



webmap.read_config(toml_path)
Read a Ribasim TOML, return the config, the input directory and the database path.



webmap.read_features(database, layer, id_column)
Read a layer whose id column is the GeoPackage FID, so GDAL does not return it as a column.



webmap.read_netcdf(source, id_dim)
Read the (time, id) variables of a Ribasim NetCDF file as float32 (id, time) arrays sorted by id.



webmap.run_info(toml_path, results_dir)
When the model was run, from ribasim.log, and from which commits, from runinfo.json next to the TOML.
Only what is known is included, so the result may be empty.



webmap.table_slug(name)
Convert a Ribasim table name like “Basin / profile” to “basin_profile”.



webmap.write_by_id(ids, times, data, id_dim, path)
Write long-format Parquet sorted by id, one row group per block of ids, for per-feature time series.



webmap.write_by_time(ids, data, id_dim, path)
Write Parquet ordered by time then id, one row group per block of time steps, for map animation.



webmap.write_parquet(df, path, row_group_size=ROW_GROUP_SIZE)
Write a DataFrame to Parquet, see write_table.



webmap.write_table(table, path, row_group_size=ROW_GROUP_SIZE)
Write zstd compressed Parquet with column statistics for row group lookup.
The float32 coordinates are stored with byte stream split, which compresses the link coordinates about 40% better than the plain encoding. The float64 input tables repeat many values, which suit dictionary encoding.

title: transboundary_inflow
text:
transboundary_inflow
Foreign inflows (buitenlandse aanvoer) on the FlowBoundaries of the regional models.
data/buitenlandse_aanvoer.csv lists each foreign inflow once: its water authority, the name of its FlowBoundary, its location and hydro-object, an optional measured timeseries, and three constant flow rates [m3/s]. For inflows with measurements, the constants are the medians over all measurements, over the summer (April to September) and over the winter (October to March), see pipeline/_preprocess_buitenlandse_aanvoer.py.
The inflows are matched to the FlowBoundaries of the meta_categorie “buitenlandse aanvoer” by name, and checked against their location. The hydro-objects are recorded to later match the inflows independently of the schematization.





Name
Description




add_transboundary_inflow
Set the measured daily flow rates of the foreign inflows of the water authority, from start to end time.


match_flow_boundaries
Match the inflows to the FlowBoundaries of the meta_categorie “buitenlandse aanvoer”, by name.


median_flow_rates
The constants of an inflow: the median flow rates of all days, of the summer and of the winter [m3/s].


read_overview
Read and check the foreign inflows of OVERVIEW_CSV, indexed by their id.


read_timeseries
Read the daily mean flow rates [m3/s] of a measured inflow, without the days without measurements.


set_constant_inflow
Set the foreign inflows of the water authority to one of their constants.

    model,
    authority,
    starttime,
    endtime,
)
Set the measured daily flow rates of the foreign inflows of the water authority, from start to end time.
Gaps in the measurements are interpolated linearly. Before the first and after the last measurement, the flow rate is constant_global. Inflows without measurements get constant_global as static flow rate.

title: seasonal_levels
text:
seasonal_levels
Summer and winter target levels (zomer- en winterpeil) in a model with one target level per Basin.
The models are built with one target level per Basin, meta_streefpeil in the Basin / area table, from which the levels of their control are derived: the thresholds of the DiscreteControl conditions on its level, and the min_upstream_level and max_downstream_level of the Outlets and Pumps around it. apply_seasonal_levels varies these over the year with the level management of the peilgebieden of ribasim_nl.peilbeheer, see https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/893:

assign_peilbeheer gives a Basin the level management of the peilgebied that covers most of its area, or of the weir near it with the closest target level. Its target level stays the same in the season of which the target level of the peilgebied is closest to it, since the target levels of the models are checked with the water boards. The peilgebied gives the difference with the other season, and the bounds of the target level. A peilgebied of which both target levels are far from that of the Basin does not describe its water, and is not assigned. join_peilbeheer gives the Basins that are joined by resistance nodes, and so are one water in the model, the level management of the largest area of them, also none.
The thresholds of the DiscreteControl conditions on the level of a Basin follow its target level. Thresholds with the default band of DEFAULT_LEVEL_THRESHOLD_RANGE around a level get the bounds of the target level instead.
The Outlets and Pumps controlled by a DiscreteControl node get a winter and a summer variant of each control state, with the levels of that season. A condition on the season switches between them.
The initial level of a Basin follows its target level at the start of the model.

The levels change at once, at the begin of the transitions between summer and winter. A gradual transition needs Ribasim to support parameters of control states that change over time. The DiscreteControl nodes that change over the year get cyclic timeseries, over the year of the start of the model.
The regional models get the seasons in ribasim_nl.regional_model.finish_regional_model. koppelen removes them with remove_seasonal_levels, since the coupling works with the fixed levels, and applies them again to the coupled model. The fixed levels and thresholds are kept in the meta_fixed_ columns for this.

title: observations
text:
observations
Add Observation nodes with measured discharges to a model.
The measurement series and the model links they are compared with are taken from the koppeltabel that is also used by ribasim_nl.analyse_results. Each series gets an Observation node at the measurement location, with the measured values. If the series is measured on a single link, the Observation node observes the flow_rate of the connector node of that link, or else of its Junction. The flow_rate of a Junction is the flow through it, the sum of its outflows. These nodes are found by their type and location, which do not change when links are renumbered. Other Observation nodes are not linked, as a reminder; meta_koppeling says why.

title: layout
text:
layout
Layout of a model on the map: nodes not on top of each other, and links without overlapping segments.
This only changes node and link geometries, which Ribasim does not use in the simulation.





Name
Description




coincident_nodes
Pairs of node ids that are within distance of each other, as an array of shape (2, n).


move_nodes
Move nodes, and the ends of their links along.


offset_junctions
Offset the Junctions to the right of the direction of the flow through them, along with their links.


offset_links
Offset links to the right of their direction, like traffic, keeping their ends at their nodes.


overlapping_links
Pairs of flow and observation link ids that overlap over more than min_length, as an array of shape (2, n).


place_bergend_nodes
Place each bergend Basin distance from its doorgaand Basin, and its connector halfway.


resolve_overlaps
Offset links that still overlap other links further to their right, see offset_links.


separate_nodes
Move nodes that are within min_distance of another node, such that no nodes are on top of each other.


tidy_layout
Make the layout of a model readable: no nodes on top of each other, and no overlapping links.





layout.coincident_nodes(model, distance)
Pairs of node ids that are within distance of each other, as an array of shape (2, n).



layout.move_nodes(model, locations)
Move nodes, and the ends of their links along.



layout.offset_junctions(model, distance=5.0, junction_ids=None)
Offset the Junctions to the right of the direction of the flow through them, along with their links.
The Junctions of the inflows and outflows of a Basin then no longer coincide. Only junction_ids are offset if given, else all Junctions.



layout.offset_links(model, distance=5.0, link_ids=None, bend=False)
Offset links to the right of their direction, like traffic, keeping their ends at their nodes.
Links that share a route in opposite directions, such as the inflows and outflows of a Basin, then no longer overlap, while links that share a route in the same direction stay together. With bend, straight links get a point halfway that is offset as well.



layout.overlapping_links(model, min_length)
Pairs of flow and observation link ids that overlap over more than min_length, as an array of shape (2, n).



layout.place_bergend_nodes(model, distance=100.0, directions=16)
Place each bergend Basin distance from its doorgaand Basin, and its connector halfway.
The direction is the one with the most room to other links and nodes, within the area of the doorgaand Basin. If no direction fits at distance, half that distance is tried, and so on, and finally also directions outside the area.











Name
Type
Description
Default




model
Model
Ribasim model, with meta_categorie “bergend” for the bergend Basins
required


distance
float
distance between the bergend and the doorgaand Basin
100.0


directions
int
number of directions to try
16







layout.resolve_overlaps(model, distance=5.0, min_length=1.0, max_iterations=5)
Offset links that still overlap other links further to their right, see offset_links.
These are for instance the links of neighboring Basins along a shared waterway.



layout.separate_nodes(model, min_distance=10.0)
Move nodes that are within min_distance of another node, such that no nodes are on top of each other.
Of two such nodes, the most movable one is moved, see MOVABLE_NODE_TYPES; Basins are never moved. It is moved to the first free location around the other node, starting in the direction away from it.



layout.tidy_layout(
    model,
    *,
    offset=5.0,
    min_distance=10.0,
    bergend_distance=100.0,
)
Make the layout of a model readable: no nodes on top of each other, and no overlapping links.
See place_bergend_nodes, offset_links, offset_junctions, separate_nodes and resolve_overlaps.

text:
geometry
Functions to apply on a shapely.geometry





Name
Description




basin_to_point
Return a representative point for the basin; centroid if it is within (Multi)Polygon or polylabel if not.


connected_parts
Split a (Multi)Polygon in the parts connected to the part that contains point, and the other parts.


drop_z
Drop the z-coordinate of a geometry if it has.


link
Create a LineString geometry between two Point geometries, dropping z-coordinate if any


polygon_parts
The polygons of a geometry that are on average wider than tolerance, so without slivers.


snap_boundaries_to_other_line
Snap the boundaries of line to the boundary or link/vertice of other_line if boundaries are within tolerance


sort_basins
Sort basins in a MultiPolygon or list of Polygons on .area in ascending order (small to large).


split_basin
Split a polygon with a line into two polygons.


split_line
Split a line into two lines based on a point.


union_polygons
The union of polygons, as shapely.union_all, but checked.





geometry.basin_to_point(basin_polygon, tolerance=None)
Return a representative point for the basin; centroid if it is within (Multi)Polygon or polylabel if not.


basin_polygon : Polygon | MultiPolygon (Multi)Polygon to get representative point for tolerance: None | float Enforce a tolerance by which the point is to be within the polygon



Point Representative point for the basin




geometry.connected_parts(geometry, point, tolerance=0.001)
Split a (Multi)Polygon in the parts connected to the part that contains point, and the other parts.
Parts at most tolerance apart are connected, also through other parts. That joins parts that versions of GEOS leave touching or a sliver apart. The connected parts are returned as Polygon if there is one.



geometry.drop_z(geometry)
Drop the z-coordinate of a geometry if it has.


geometry : LineString | MultiPolygon | Point | Polygon Input geometry



LineString | Point | Polygon | MultiPolygon Output geometry




geometry.link(point_from, point_to)
Create a LineString geometry between two Point geometries, dropping z-coordinate if any
Args: point_from (Point): description point_to (Point): description


LineString: LineString without z-coordinate




geometry.polygon_parts(geometry, tolerance=0.0)
The polygons of a geometry that are on average wider than tolerance, so without slivers.
The average width of a polygon is taken as its area divided by its perimeter.



geometry.snap_boundaries_to_other_line(line, other_line, tolerance=0.1)
Snap the boundaries of line to the boundary or link/vertice of other_line if boundaries are within tolerance



geometry.sort_basins(basin_polygons)
Sort basins in a MultiPolygon or list of Polygons on .area in ascending order (small to large).


basin_polygons : MultiPolygon | list[Polygon] MultiPolygon or list of polygons to be sorted



MultiPolygon | list[Polygon] MultiPolygon with sorted polygons




geometry.split_basin(basin_polygon, line)
Split a polygon with a line into two polygons.
Credits to https://kuanbutts.com/2020/07/07/subdivide-polygon-with-linestring/


basin_polygon : Polygon Polygon to cut into two line : LineString Cutline fro the Polygon



MultiPolygon Multipolygon with two polygons




geometry.split_line(line, point, *, tolerance=0.1)
Split a line into two lines based on a point.
As the built-in shapely.ops.split is not designed to do this splitting, its use should be avoided.
This line-splitting function uses the splitting point as part of the newly generated lines.
Args: line (LineString): line to be split point (Point): point to mark split-location tolerance (float, optional): tolerance of distance from point to line, defaults to 0.1.


tuple[LineString] | tuple[LineString, LineString]: a tuple of one or two LineString-objects




geometry.union_polygons(polygons, tolerance=0.001)
The union of polygons, as shapely.union_all, but checked.
GEOS can lose or add whole parts in a union with slivers. A union is wrong if it exceeds the area of the polygons together by more than tolerance times their perimeter, or is further than tolerance from a point inside a polygon that is not a sliver, on average wider than 100 times tolerance. Then the union is taken again with a fixed precision of tolerance, or if that fails, without slivers.

title: design_capacities
text:
design_capacities
Set the unknown capacities of Pumps and Outlets from the area they drain or supply.
This uses the same design discharges and supply as the parametrization of the vrij afwaterend models, see ribasim_nl.parametrization.static_data_xlsx.defaults: per day, a drainage Pump discharges 15 mm and a drainage Outlet 50 mm over the area it drains, and a supplying Pump or Outlet supplies 4 mm over the area downstream. The drainage of each water body is split over the drains out of it, and each node is limited by what can flow into and out of the water bodies around it.





Name
Description




design_capacities
Compute the design capacity of each Pump and Outlet in function_table from the area it drains or supplies.


known_capacities
Get the largest max_flow_rate by node_id of the Pumps and Outlets with meta_known_flow_rate.


set_design_capacities
Set the unknown capacities of the Pumps and Outlets to their design capacity, see design_capacities.





design_capacities.design_capacities(model, function_table)
Compute the design capacity of each Pump and Outlet in function_table from the area it drains or supplies.
A drain node gets its share of the drainage of the water body it comes from, see _split_drainage, and a supply node the area of the Basins downstream, up to the drain nodes. A flow_control node passes water in both directions, and gets the larger of both. A supply node that supplies no Basin, such as one out of the model, supplies the area upstream instead. The area of bergend Basins is left out, as it is the same as that of their doorgaand Basin. Finally the capacities are limited by the nodes around them, see _limit_by_neighbours.


model : Model The model, with the Basin areas, and Pump and Outlet static tables with a meta_known_flow_rate column. function_table : pd.DataFrame The function of the Pumps and Outlets by node_id: drain, supply or flow_control, see ribasim_nl.control.add_function_to_peilbeheerst_node_table.



pd.DataFrame By node_id, the drained and supplied area in m2, the design capacity from that area, and the capacity limited by the nodes around it, in m3/s.




design_capacities.known_capacities(model)
Get the largest max_flow_rate by node_id of the Pumps and Outlets with meta_known_flow_rate.



design_capacities.set_design_capacities(model, function_table)
Set the unknown capacities of the Pumps and Outlets to their design capacity, see design_capacities.
Capacities are known where meta_known_flow_rate is set in the static table; these are kept, as are those of nodes that drain or supply no Basin. The flow_rate of all nodes is set to their max_flow_rate, except in the control states that switch them off.


model : Model The model, with Pump and Outlet static tables with a meta_known_flow_rate column. function_table : pd.DataFrame The function of the Pumps and Outlets by node_id: drain, supply or flow_control, see ribasim_nl.control.add_function_to_peilbeheerst_node_table.



pd.DataFrame The design capacities, see design_capacities, and whether each capacity was known.

Set the unknown capacities of the Pumps and Outlets to their design capacity, see design_capacities.





design_capacities.design_capacities(model, function_table)
Compute the design capacity of each Pump and Outlet in function_table from the area it drains or supplies.
A drain node gets its share of the drainage of the water body it comes from, see _split_drainage, and a supply node the area of the Basins downstream, up to the drain nodes. A flow_control node passes water in both directions, and gets the larger of both. A supply node that supplies no Basin, such as one out of the model, supplies the area upstream instead. The area of bergend Basins is left out, as it is the same as that of their doorgaand Basin. Finally the capacities are limited by the nodes around them, see _limit_by_neighbours.
