title: Model viewer
text:
The Model viewer shows the input and results of the coupled LHM model (lhm_coupled) of main on a web map. It is a static web app: the docs site serves only the JavaScript, and the browser reads the model data directly from MinIO. The model of a pull request can be previewed too, together with its differences from main, at https://ribasim.nl/viewer?pr=<number>. Any other published version can be viewed, or compared with another, by its commit, see Links to a version.
The Water authority choice above the layer list shows the nodes and links of one authority, by the waterbeheercode their node ids start with, see ribasim_nl.aquo. It also shows the links to other authorities and the nodes at their other end, such as the regional inlets and outlets of the hws, and the Basin / areas of the shown Basins. The choice is kept in the URL, as #authority=<waterbeheercode>.
flowchart LR
  A[modellen/lhm_coupled] -->|dvc repro run_lhm_coupled| R[runs/lhm_coupled]
  R -->|dvc repro export_webmap| B[webmap/lhm_coupled]
  B -->|pixi run publish-webmap| C[MinIO doc-image/webmap]
  C --> D[Model viewer page]
  L[dvc.lock on GitHub main] --> D
All local paths are relative to data/Rijkswaterstaat.

title: Model viewer
text:
Fit to the measurements
The Observations choice in the time bar colors the Observation nodes by how well the simulated values fit their measurements, see ribasim_nl.goodness_of_fit:

KGE and NSE: the Kling-Gupta and Nash-Sutcliffe efficiencies over the whole run, from purple at -1 to green at 1. At 0 the results are as good as the mean of the measurements.
bias: the difference of the mean simulated and measured value, relative to the mean absolute measurement. It is green within 25%, the limit of a satisfactory bias of discharges of Moriasi et al. (2007), grey at 50%, and purple from 100% either way.
simulated − observed: the difference at the time of the time bar, from red for too low to blue for too high. It is colored on a symmetric log scale, since the differences of large rivers and small ditches span orders of magnitude.

The efficiencies and bias need 365 days with both a measured and a simulated value, so Observation nodes with fewer days, or without a measurement at the time of the time bar, are small grey dots. Change the limits of a color scale in its legend. The Observations box above the layer list lists the shown Observation nodes by their fit, the best or the worst first, with the median, and zooms to one when clicked. The panel of an Observation node shows its fit above the chart of its observed and simulated values.

title: Model viewer
text:
Updating the published data

Run the model with the run_lhm_coupled DVC stage. It copies the model of modellen/lhm_coupled to runs/lhm_coupled, and writes the results of the first 2 of its 3 years next to it. It also writes the commit of the code to runinfo.json, which the viewer shows next to the scale bar, with the time the run finished from results/ribasim.log. For now this runs with a looser solver tolerance, see pipeline/run_lhm_coupled.py. The NetCDF results are compressed, to save space in DVC. This takes about 1.5 hours, so normally pull the cached results instead:
pixi run dvc pull run_lhm_coupled
Export the model to web-friendly files with the export_webmap DVC stage, which takes about 10 minutes:
pixi run dvc repro --pull --single-item export_webmap
This writes data/Rijkswaterstaat/webmap/lhm_coupled, see ribasim_nl.webmap for details:



File
Content




nodes.parquet
Node table with all attributes and lon/lat


links.parquet
Link table with all attributes and simplified geometry


basin_area.pmtiles
Basin / area polygons as vector tiles


waterboards.geojson
Simplified water board boundaries


tables/*.parquet
All other input tables, including those in NetCDF, sorted by node_id


results/*_by_id.parquet
Basin and flow results sorted by id, for the time series charts


results/*_by_time.parquet
Basin level and storage, and flow rate, ordered by time step, for coloring the map


results/observation_metrics.parquet
How well the results fit the measurements of each Observation node, see Fit to the measurements


results/observation_by_time.parquet
The difference simulated − observed of each Observation node, ordered by time step, for coloring the map


manifest.json
List of the files above with their content hash and size, the color scale of each result variable, and when and from which commit the model was run



Results are only exported if the model’s results directory exists. DVC does not cache this output, since the published model on MinIO is a copy of it already. dvc.lock does record its hash, which names the published model.
Push the run and commit the updated dvc.lock, see DVC:
pixi run dvc push run_lhm_coupled
Publish the model as a preview of the pull request of the current branch. This needs credentials with write access in .env, and the GitHub CLI gh, logged in.
pixi run publish-webmap
This uploads the model of the working tree, and that of origin/main, which it fetches first, and their differences, see Comparing models. It then adds a comment to the pull request with the link https://ribasim.nl/viewer?pr=<number> and a summary of the differences, or updates that comment on later publishes. Use --pr <number> to publish for another pull request, and --main to only publish the model of origin/main. Use --commit <revision> to publish the model of a commit on GitHub, and add --base <revision> to also publish its differences from another commit, see Links to a version.

pixi run repro-local runs steps 1, 2 and 4 by default, and with --push it also pushes the run, see Running locally. The docs do not need to be rebuilt to show another model.

How the published models are found
Everything is uploaded to the anonymously readable doc-image/webmap/ prefix on MinIO, see ribasim_nl.webmap_publish:







Object
Content




files/<hash>.<ext>
The exported files, named by their content hash, so unchanged files are uploaded once and shared by all models


lhm_coupled/snapshots/<md5>/manifest.json
The manifest of an export, named by the DVC hash of the export_webmap output in dvc.lock


lhm_coupled/main.json
The snapshot of the latest published main


lhm_coupled/diffs/<base md5>-<head md5>.json
The differences between two snapshots


lhm_coupled/prs/<number>.json
The snapshots of a pull request and the main it was compared with, and their differences



To show main, the viewer reads dvc.lock from main on GitHub, and loads the snapshot of its export_webmap output. So once a pull request whose model was published is merged, the viewer shows its model, without publishing again. If that snapshot is not published, for instance because a pull request changed the model without publishing it, the viewer shows the snapshot in main.json with a warning. The next pixi run publish-webmap then exports the run of main again, and publishes it. Likewise, to compare a pull request with main, the export of main is downloaded from its snapshot, or exported again from its run if it is not published. For a pull request, the viewer warns if main changed since the model was published; publish again to compare with the latest main. Snapshots and files that are no longer used are not deleted.


Links to a version
Node and link IDs change between versions of the model, so a link to a node in an issue would show another node later. The viewer therefore puts the commit of the model it shows in the page URL, so a copied link keeps showing that version:







URL
Model




viewer
The latest main, then pinned to viewer?commit=<commit>


viewer?commit=<commit>
The model of a commit on GitHub, by the snapshot in its dvc.lock


viewer?base=<commit>&commit=<commit>
The model of a commit, compared with that of another commit


viewer?pr=<number>
The latest published model of a pull request, compared with its base


&compare=0
Added to a comparison: only the model, without its comparison



Commits may be shortened; pinned links use 10 characters. The view and selection after # are kept. If a pinned model is no longer that of the latest main, the viewer says so, with a link to the latest main at the same place. The viewer knows the commit of main since the docs are built and published for each push to main, so after a merge it shows the previous main until that is done. Links to a pull request are not pinned, since it is usually published before its dvc.lock is committed.
Two commits can be compared if their differences are published, for instance to see what changed in a month. Since snapshots and differences are named by the DVC hashes of the models, any two commits with the models of a published comparison can be compared, like main before and after a pull request. To compare other commits, publish their models and differences:
pixi run publish-webmap --commit origin/main --base <commit>
This prints the link to the comparison. A model that is not published is exported again from its run in DVC.

title: Model viewer
text:
Viewing local models
The viewer can also show any local model, without publishing it:
pixi run viewer data/Rijkswaterstaat/modellen/hws_2025_10_1/hws.toml
This exports the model with ribasim_nl.webmap to .cache/viewer, serves it with the viewer on http://localhost:8000, and opens it in a web browser. The export is reused as long as the model, its results and the export code are unchanged, so only the first run takes long; about 10 minutes for the coupled LHM model with results. Results are shown if the model’s results directory exists. Use --port to serve on another port, and --no-browser to not open a browser.

Comparing models
To review a pull request that changes a model, view only the differences from another version of the model. Usually that is the same model at another git revision, like main:
pixi run viewer data/Rijkswaterstaat/runs/lhm_coupled/lhm_coupled.toml --base origin/main
--base takes a git revision or the TOML of another model. The model at a revision is read with DVC, from the DVC cache or the DVC remote, into .cache/viewer/revisions. Add --rev to also take the viewed model from a git revision instead of the working tree, for instance --rev HEAD --base origin/main. Fetch first to compare with the latest origin/main.
Nodes are matched by id, and links by their from and to node, since links get renumbered, see ribasim_nl.webmap_diff. A node or link in both models is changed if its geometry, an attribute, its rows in an input table, or its Basin / area differ. Initial Basin levels in Basin / state that differ less than 1 cm are equal, since every run of the regional models changes them slightly, see TABLE_TOLERANCES in ribasim_nl.webmap_diff. The map shows only the added, removed and changed features, in the colors of their status: green, orange and purple, on a grey base map. When zoomed out, the status rings around changed nodes become small dots. Removed and changed Basin / areas of the old model are drawn as dashed outlines. Turn on Unchanged in the layer list to show the other features faintly, for context. Observation nodes and their links are always shown, also when unchanged or filtered out in the Differences box, so their charts can be compared; the observed values are charted with the simulated values of both models. The simulated values of the base model are those of the observed node in the base model, also if its links were renumbered or lead to renumbered nodes.
If both models have results, the Basin levels and flow rates are compared too. Basins and flow links whose results differ more than a tolerance are also shown, in shades of grey by the largest difference. Differences of up to 1 mm in level, and of up to 1 L/s plus 1% in flow rate, are ignored as solver noise.
The Differences box counts the differences by status and by what changed, for instance Basin / state or geometry. Its View without differences link shows the model normally, at the same place, by adding &compare=0 to the URL. Uncheck a status or a change to hide those features from the map, for instance to look past the many changed initial states. It also lists the changed TOML settings, all differing features, and the features whose results differ, largest first; click one to zoom to it. The panel of a changed feature lists what changed, shows the old value of changed attributes struck through, and shows both versions of changed tables. The result charts show the old model as dashed lines in a lighter tint.
If both models have the fit to the measurements, the time bar has the Observations choice only, which can also color the Observation nodes by the change of their KGE, NSE or absolute bias, from purple for a worse to green for a better fit. The panel of an Observation node shows the fit of both models.

title: Model viewer
text:
Developing the viewer
The viewer lives in viewer/ and is written in TypeScript, built with Vite. It uses MapLibre GL JS for the basemap and the Basin / area tiles, deck.gl to draw the nodes and links, and hyparquet to read Parquet files with HTTP range requests.
Start a development server that serves your local export_webmap output, and open http://localhost:5173:
pixi run viewer-dev
Changes to the TypeScript code reload the page automatically. pixi run viewer-build checks types and builds the viewer into docs/viewer-app. pixi run docs and pixi run docs-render run it before rendering the docs. Add ?data=<url> to the viewer page URL to load the data from another location, and &base_data=<url>&diff=<url> to compare it with another model, for instance ?data=http://localhost:5173/ to use the development server. Only the default MinIO host, the docs site itself and localhost are accepted.

title: Testing
text:
Run the repository checks before submitting changes:
This also runs on CI. It runs the linter, the formatter, the type checker and other hooks.
The tests are in src/ribasim_nl/tests, src/hydamo/tests and scripts/test_*.py, and also run on CI:

title: Testing
text:
Model input validation
Model.validate_ribasim_nl() runs extensible checks on model input and supplements Ribasim schema validation. Add project-wide input rules to ribasim_nl.validation.validate_model.

title: Testing
text:
Result regression testing
The dry and wet steady-state scenarios guard against a Basin losing its ability to maintain its water level. The forcing_* DVC stages of the level controlled models, also in repro.sh, run and check the dry and wet models. The bergend_* stages of the gravity controlled models write them, and run and check them only with MODEL_EXEC = True in their 04_add_full_control.py, which is off in the pipeline. A Basin is steady-state when its final water level differs by at most 0.01 m from the mean of the final 24 hours and its storage remains positive throughout the simulation.
Known level-instability exceptions are kept as explicit scenario-specific Basin node IDs in ribasim_nl.steady_state_regression. Exceptions do not bypass the positive-storage check, and an exception for a missing Basin ID fails the run.
Scenario results are available for inspection in each model’s results directory, including output_controle.gpkg and output_controle.qlr.

title: Testing
text:
Coupled model result checks
The validate_lhm_coupled DVC stage checks the results of run_lhm_coupled for large regressions, with ribasim_nl.result_validation. It takes a few seconds, so after pulling the results it can be run with:
pixi run dvc repro --single-item validate_lhm_coupled
It summarizes the run in metrics, and checks them against the loose limits in LIMITS:

solver: the number of right-hand side calls, the mean timestep and the 5th percentile of the mean timestep per day, and the fraction of rejected timesteps.
observations: the number of Observation nodes that are compared with the simulated flow rate of the node they observe, and their median Nash-Sutcliffe (NSE) and Kling-Gupta efficiencies (KGE).
discharge_kge: the KGE of the discharge at key points of the main water system, such as the Rhine branches and the sluices of the Afsluitdijk.
level_p01 and level_p99: the 1st and 99th percentile of the levels of key Basins, such as the IJsselmeer and the Noordzeekanaal.

The metrics are written to data/Rijkswaterstaat/metrics/lhm_coupled.json, which is tracked by git, so a pull request shows how they changed, and the comparison per Observation node to lhm_coupled_observations.csv next to it. Compare the metrics with those of main with:
pixi run dvc metrics diff main
The metrics also include the computation time in hours, but it is not checked, since it depends on the machine and its load. The other solver metrics hardly do, so they catch slowdowns more reliably. If a change of the results is intended, change LIMITS in the same pull request and explain why.

title: Testing
text:
Completed-model result checks
Control.run() exports selected result metrics to results/output_controle.gpkg. It defaults to DYNAMIC_FORCING_METRICS; use STATIC_FORCING_METRICS or AFVOER_METRICS for the other established workflows, or pass a custom metric set. Call Control.validate_result_conditions() after export to enforce conditions. It logs every violation with its Basin node ID before raising one error, so all failures can be addressed together.
New completed-model checks belong on Control and can be called after future dynamic model exports without changing the dry/wet scenario runner.

Allowing a known exception
Only after reviewing an intentional model change, add the Basin node ID to ALLOWED_NON_STEADY_STATE_NODE_IDS for its authority and scenario. Remove an exception once the Basin becomes steady-state again.

title: Co-development with Ribasim
text:
Ribasim-NL pins to a specific commit of Ribasim in pixi.toml, often of a branch for this project, with a matching build of the core in scripts/install_ribasim_core.py. During development sometimes you may want to test out the latest unreleased development version of Ribasim.
To do so, open pixi.toml in your editor. Find the [pypi-dependencies] section and change the ribasim git source:
[pypi-dependencies]
ribasim = { git = "https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim", branch = "main", subdirectory = "python/ribasim" }
You can change the branch name if needed, or use a specific commit with rev = "0075d4a".
If you are making changes to the Ribasim repository yourself, it will be more convenient to point to a local clone rather than GitHub. This can be done using this syntax:
[pypi-dependencies]
ribasim = { path = "../Ribasim/python/ribasim", editable = true }
This path will work if you clone Ribasim next to Ribasim-NL.
After you are done modifying pixi.toml, run pixi install to ensure the dependencies are installed.
The Ribasim core binary is installed separately by pixi run install-core, see scripts/install_ribasim_core.py. pixi run repro-local runs it first, so a run always uses the core configured there. Make sure its version is compatible with the Ribasim Python package.
For Ribasim developer documentation see ribasim.org/dev.

title: Reproducing pull requests
text:
A full reproduction of the pipeline takes hours, so pull requests that change the model are often open, and reproduced, at the same time. Each reproduction changes dvc.lock and the metrics in data/Rijkswaterstaat/metrics/lhm_coupled.json, so two such pull requests conflict once one of them is merged. This page describes how to handle that without rerunning anything.
The run of a pull request serves two purposes:
Therefore dvc.lock on main is the latest reproduced state, which may lag behind the code on main. Regular catch-up runs reproduce main again, for all pull requests merged since the previous run at once.

title: Reproducing pull requests
section: A pull request that changes the model
text:
A pull request that changes the model

Reproduce the pipeline on the branch, and push its outputs to the DVC remote, see Running locally:
pixi run repro-local --push
Commit and push dvc.lock and the metrics. Describe the effect in the pull request, compared with the base of the run:
pixi run dvc metrics diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
Merge. If dvc.lock on main changed since the base of the run, merge main into the branch and keep the dvc.lock and metrics of main, without rerunning:
git merge origin/main
git checkout origin/main -- dvc.lock data/Rijkswaterstaat/metrics/lhm_coupled.json
git commit
Keep those of main even if git merges dvc.lock without conflicts, and never combine the two by hand: a dvc.lock that mixes two runs describes outputs that no run produced. Always take dvc.lock and the metrics together, so they belong to the same run.

The pull request is then merged without its run being recorded on main, until the next catch-up run. Its outputs stay on the DVC remote, and its preview in the model viewer remains available.

title: Reproducing pull requests
section: Push the outputs of every run
text:
Push the outputs of every run
Push the outputs of every run whose dvc.lock is committed, with --push or pixi run dvc push, also on pull requests:

The dvc.lock of a pull request may end up on main, and the outputs of main must always be on the remote, since every reproduction pulls its inputs from there.
Reviewers can pull the model of a pull request, see Get data.
The model viewer exports the model of a commit again from its run, if that export is not published yet.

Outputs that did not change are not uploaded again, since the remote stores files by their content.

title: Reproducing pull requests
text:
Catch-up runs on main
When main has merged pull requests that are not reproduced, a catch-up run reproduces it and opens a pull request named “Reproduce the pipeline on top of main” with the run:
pixi run repro-main
This runs in a worktree dedicated to it, and is normally started every night by a systemd timer, see below. It:

Waits while a catch-up pull request is open, unless dvc.lock on main changed since its run. Then it closes it, since pull requests keep the dvc.lock of main.
Skips a commit of main that it attempted before, also when that failed, unless given --force. It also skips while another catch-up run is busy, but not for runs of other pull requests, which go in the next catch-up run.
Runs pixi run repro-local --incremental --push on main, which first installs the Ribasim core of scripts/install_ribasim_core.py if that changed. Since every stage depends on the ribasim_nl package, this usually reruns most of the pipeline. With --full it runs all stages, see below.
If dvc.lock changed, pushes the run to a new branch repro-main-<date>-<time>, opens the pull request, publishes its model viewer preview, and the figures of the docs.
Has Claude describe the effect with the describe-run skill in .claude/skills, which can only read files, and not the credentials. The skill is also useful to describe the run of any other pull request.

Review and merge the pull request yourself, like any other one.
To redo the catch-up run of a commit, for instance when it ran with the wrong environment, run all stages in the worktree of the timer:
git fetch origin main
git checkout --detach origin/main
pixi run repro-main --force --full

The nightly timer
On a Linux workstation with enough cores and memory, install the timer with:
pixi run install-repro-main
This creates the worktree next to the main checkout, set up with pixi run setup-worktree, and enables a systemd user timer that runs pixi run repro-main there at 01:13; use --time HH:MM for another time, and --uninstall to remove it. The service resets the worktree to origin/main before each run, and refuses to do so in any other checkout. If it fails, it shows a desktop notification. Follow it with journalctl --user -fu ribasim-nl-repro-main, start it right away with systemctl --user start --no-block ribasim-nl-repro-main, and stop it with systemctl --user stop ribasim-nl-repro-main.
The service runs the code of main unattended, with your credentials: the MinIO key in .env, gh, and claude. It runs without new privileges and creates files that only you can read. It only pushes to repro-main-* branches and never merges, and it checks that the description it publishes contains no credentials. To limit what it can do on GitHub, give it a fine-grained token for Deltares/Ribasim-NL only, with read and write access to contents and pull requests, in ~/.config/ribasim-nl/repro-main.env, readable by you only:
GH_TOKEN=github_pat_...
The timer only fires while you are logged in, unless you run loginctl enable-linger. Without a session the gh credentials in the keyring are locked, so then the token above is needed.

title: Reproducing pull requests
text:
Stacked pull requests
Stack a pull request on top of another one when it builds on it, or to see their combined effect. It is often enough to reproduce only the top of the stack. The model viewer compares each pull request in a stack with the one below it, so it only shows its own changes.
Pull requests are squash merged, so the commits of a pull request in the stack are not on main after it is merged, only a new commit with the same changes. Merge a stack in one of two ways:

Top down, as one commit on main: squash merge the top pull request into the branch below it, repeat until the bottom, and squash merge that into main. This never conflicts, and main gets the dvc.lock of the top, which belongs to the code of the whole stack.
Bottom up, as one commit per pull request: once the bottom is merged, GitHub deletes its branch and bases the next pull request on main. That pull request still contains the commits of the merged one, which conflict wherever it changed the same lines again, always in dvc.lock. Replay only its own commits on main, starting after the last commit of the merged pull request, here number 123:
git fetch origin main
git rebase --onto origin/main $(gh pr view 123 --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)
git push --force-with-lease
If the bottom pull request kept the dvc.lock of main, the rebase stops at the commit with the run of the next pull request. Then keep the dvc.lock and metrics of main, as described above.

title: Contributing
text: Ribasim-NL welcomes contributions.

title: Contributing
text:
Clone Ribasim-NL
In order to have the Ribasim-NL repository locally available, you can clone it with Git. Git can be installed from git-scm.com. Once installed, run the following command at a directory of your choice:
git clone https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL.git
To continue with the following steps, make the root of the repository your working directory by running
cd Ribasim-NL

title: Contributing
text:
Install Pixi
Install Pixi as described in the Pixi documentation. Pixi manages all dependencies; always run commands through it, for example pixi run python path/to/script.py.

title: Contributing
text:
Add your access key
The project data and the Ribasim core binary are stored on Deltares MinIO (S3) storage. To access them you need an access key. Ask a repository maintainer for a read-only key. Maintainers create one key per institute in the MinIO console, restricted with this policy.
Copy the template .env.default in the root of the repository to .env:
cp .env.default .env
Then fill in your key, using single quotes around the values:
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID='<access key>'
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY='<secret key>'
The .env file is gitignored, since it contains secrets. Pixi loads it automatically for every pixi run command. The other variables can normally keep their defaults, see Other settings.

title: Contributing
text:
Install the environment
Set up the full development environment by running:
pixi run install
This installs the Python environment, the Git hooks, and the Ribasim core binary in bin/ribasim. It does not download project data; see Get data.






Note



In a new git worktree, run pixi run setup-worktree instead. It shares the .env and the DVC cache of the main checkout, and installs the Ribasim core. Do not run pixi run install there: it points the Git hooks, which all worktrees share, to that worktree.


The first time you open the Ribasim-NL repo in Visual Studio Code, the pixi-code extension should automatically detect the Pixi environment and configure the Python interpreter.
If you encounter issues, try running pixi clean and running pixi run install again.

title: Contributing
text:
Get data
The data is versioned with DVC, a tool that works like Git for large data files. You don’t need to know DVC to get started: download only the data you need, for instance the latest nationwide coupled model and its results:
pixi run dvc pull run_lhm_coupled
This fills data/Rijkswaterstaat/runs/lhm_coupled with the model input and its results. Open data/Rijkswaterstaat/runs/lhm_coupled/lhm_coupled.toml to see the model together with its results.
The DVC page explains how to get the data for a specific step of the pipeline, and how to rerun it.

title: Contributing
text:
Git hooks
We use prek instead of pre-commit for git hooks. It is installed as part of pixi run install, but you can also install hooks manually:
pixi run prek install -f
To run all hooks on all files manually:
pixi run check
See Testing for the tests, and Documentation for this website.

title: Contributing
text:
Other settings
Besides the access key, .env can hold these optional settings, read in src/ribasim_nl/ribasim_nl/settings.py:



Environment variable
Description




RIBASIM_NL_DATA_DIR
Local directory for data files, data by default


D3D_HOME
Root of the Delft3D installation, only needed for Delwaq


RIBASIM_NL_CLOUD_PASS
Password for the legacy Good Cloud storage, which 9 parameterized stages use to download GKW data that is not local; most users can leave it empty


OVERWRITE_FILES_FROM_CLOUD
Whether legacy Good Cloud downloads overwrite local files, true by default



Values from .env take precedence over environment variables set in your OS or terminal.

title: Documentation
text:
This website is made with Quarto from the docs folder, and published to ribasim.nl from main by the workflow .github/workflows/docs.yml.
Quarto silently finds no pages if the repository is below a hidden folder, such as a worktree in .claude/worktrees. Render a copy elsewhere in that case.

title: Documentation
text:
Diagrams
Use Mermaid for diagrams of steps and flows, in a {mermaid} code block, with short labels. The theme is set in docs/_quarto.yml. pixi run dvc-dag makes the full graph of the pipeline in docs/dev/_dvc-dag.mmd.

title: Documentation
text:
Figures
The maps and charts of real examples are not in Git, and CI has no access to the data they are made from. scripts/docs_figures.py makes them, and uploads them to doc-image/figures on MinIO, next to the other images of the docs. The pages link to them there, so the docs do not need to be rebuilt to show new figures.
Every catch-up run publishes them after it has opened its pull request, so they follow the code of main:
pixi run docs-figures --pull --publish
If that fails, the catch-up run continues and logs it, and the docs keep the previous figures. A figure that fails does not stop the others.
To work on a figure, make it locally in data/docs_figures, without uploading it:
pixi run docs-figures lumping         # one group, from the data you have
pixi run docs-figures --pull lumping  # pull its data first, as listed in the script
--publish needs credentials with write access in .env, and overwrites the figures on the live site, so only use it for a run of main. A new figure needs its name in the outputs of its group; scripts/test_docs_figures.py checks that the pages only link to figures that are made.
Captions are written by hand, and do not follow the figures. Keep them general where the figure can change, and check the numbers in those of Lumping when its data changes.

title: Documentation
text:
API reference
quartodoc builds the API reference from the docstrings, in the sections of docs/_quarto.yml.

title: Cloud storage
text: The project data and models are versioned with DVC on MinIO. The project used to store them on The Good Cloud, and the class ribasim_nl.CloudStorage still has that name, see the API reference.

title: Cloud storage
text:
Paths
Most code uses CloudStorage to find local paths under RIBASIM_NL_DATA_DIR:
from ribasim_nl import CloudStorage

cloud = CloudStorage()

verwerkt = cloud.joinpath("Delfland", "verwerkt")
model_dir = cloud.model_dir("Delfland", "forcing")

title: Cloud storage
text:
The Good Cloud






Warning



The rest of this page is about the legacy storage. It is not the main storage method for current workflows: use MinIO through DVC instead, with the credentials of the developer setup.


The Good Cloud needs the password RIBASIM_NL_CLOUD_PASS in .env, which is only shared among project collaborators, since not all input data is public.
The pipeline still has one use for it: if data/Basisgegevens/GKW is not local, which is not versioned with DVC, the parameterized stages of 9 water authorities download it from there, see ribasim_nl.gkw.
# what is available
cloud.source_data
cloud.water_authorities

# download national data
cloud.download_basisgegevens(bronnen=["PBL_watertypenkaart"])

# download the data of a water authority: delivered, processed, or both
cloud.download_aangeleverd("Rijkswaterstaat")
cloud.download_verwerkt("Rijkswaterstaat")
cloud.download_all("Rijkswaterstaat")

# upload processed data
cloud.upload_verwerkt("Rijkswaterstaat", overwrite=True)

# see which models have been uploaded, and upload a new version of the `ijsselmeer` model
cloud.uploaded_models("Rijkswaterstaat")
cloud.upload_model("Rijkswaterstaat", model="ijsselmeer")

title: DVC (Data Version Control)
text:
We use DVC to version-control large data files (models, input datasets) without storing them in Git. Git only stores small fingerprints of the data, in dvc.lock and .dvc files; the data itself lives on MinIO storage.
DVC also describes how the data is made: the pipeline in dvc.yaml is a list of stages, each a Python script with its input and output files. Most stages build the model of one water authority, and later stages combine them into the nationwide model.

title: DVC (Data Version Control)
text:
In short
You only need a few commands, always run through Pixi so your access key from .env is used (see Add your access key):







Goal
Command




Download a file or folder
pixi run dvc pull <path>


Download the inputs of a stage, e.g. rwzi
pixi run dvc pull rwzi --with-deps


Rerun a stage after changing its script
pixi run dvc repro --pull rwzi


See which stages are out of date
pixi run dvc status



The sections below explain these in more detail.






Note



Existing clones may still have remote credentials in .dvc/config.local. Remove those credential fields after migrating .env from MINIO_ACCESS_KEY and MINIO_SECRET_KEY to AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

title: DVC (Data Version Control)
text:
Pull data
Prefer pulling only the data needed for the stage you are working on. To fetch a stage and its dependencies without reproducing it, use dvc pull:
pixi run dvc pull rwzi --with-deps
To fetch the cached coupled LHM model with its results, without --with-deps, which would pull all regional models:
pixi run dvc pull run_lhm_coupled
The final cached outputs for (for example) Aa en Maas and Amstel, Gooi en Vecht can likewise be pulled directly:
pixi run dvc pull data/AaenMaas/modellen/AaenMaas_dynamic_model/
pixi run dvc pull data/AmstelGooienVecht/modellen/AmstelGooienVecht_forcing/
Only pull all tracked data when you have enough disk space (currently ~100GB), time, and just want all data local:
pixi run dvc pull
If you have local changes that you want to overwrite, add --force.

title: DVC (Data Version Control)
text:
Remotes
The MinIO remote is configured in .dvc/config:








Remote
URL
Purpose




minio (default)
s3://ribasim-nl/dvc
Primary DVC cache on MinIO

title: DVC (Data Version Control)
text:
Pipeline
The DVC pipeline is defined in dvc.yaml. Each stage depends on its scripts, its input data, and the src/ribasim_nl/ribasim_nl package as a whole. Every stage imports most of this package, so a change to it marks all stages as changed. That sometimes reruns a stage that did not need it, but never skips one whose code changed.

title: DVC (Data Version Control)
text:
Reproduce stages
During development, reproduce only the stage you are working on. The --pull option asks DVC to fetch missing dependencies before running the stage with dvc repro:
pixi run dvc repro --pull rwzi
Without --pull, dvc repro only uses data already present in the workspace or local DVC cache. Other useful options are --force to run a stage even when DVC considers it unchanged and --single-item to run only the named stage without reproducing its upstream dependencies.






Warning



A full pixi run dvc repro runs all stages one by one and takes several days. Run full reproductions in parallel instead, on a workstation with pixi run repro-local, see Running locally, or on the SLURM cluster with repro.sh, see Running on SLURM.

title: DVC (Data Version Control)
text:
Pushing changes
After producing new outputs (running pipeline stages or adding new data), push to the remote:
pixi run dvc push
Do this before pushing the updated dvc.lock file to Git, so the data hashes referenced therein are available to everyone.
Most MinIO access keys handed out are read-only. Reach out if you need help uploading data. See Reproducing pull requests for how the full runs of pull requests and of main are recorded.

title: Running locally
text:
On a workstation with enough cores and memory, the pipeline can be reproduced in parallel with:
This is the local counterpart of repro.sh. It runs validate_lhm_coupled and export_webmap and everything upstream of them, except frozen stages. So beyond the stages that repro.sh runs, it also makes the input models, and runs run_lhm_coupled, validate_lhm_coupled and export_webmap. The stages and their commands are taken from dvc.yaml. It:
Like repro.sh, it runs the stage commands directly, not with dvc repro, since parallel dvc repro processes would contend for the DVC lock. The output of each stage is written to logs/repro/<timestamp>/<stage>.log, and a summary with the status and duration of each stage is printed at the end.

title: Running locally
text:
Options

Targets: stages to reproduce together with their upstream stages, validate_lhm_coupled and export_webmap by default. For example, pixi run repro-local koppelen only builds the coupled model, like repro.sh.
--jobs N: the maximum number of stages that run at once, 12 by default. Each stage is a Python process that may also run Ribasim, so watch the memory use when increasing it.
--stagger SECONDS: the minimum time between stage starts, 30 by default, to not overload the GoodCloud server from which parameterized stages download GKW data that is not local.
--incremental: only run the stages that DVC reports as changed, and everything downstream of them, rather than all stages. Data that is not in the workspace does not count as changed, so a fresh worktree does not rerun everything. A stage that failed before only runs again if the outputs it left differ from dvc.lock. Run pixi run dvc pull first if the workspace may be behind dvc.lock.
--push: run dvc push for the reproduced stages if they all succeeded.
--no-publish: do not publish the model to the model viewer.

To keep the run going after closing the terminal, start it in for instance tmux or with nohup.

title: Reproducing models
text: Many scripts refer to the nodes, links and areas of a model by their ID, row number or geometry: the 01_fix_model.py scripts and model_edits.gpkg files of the gravity controlled models, and the feedback forms of the level controlled models. A model that is rebuilt from its source data must therefore get the same IDs, or all these references break. This page describes how the input models of the gravity controlled (#903) and level controlled models were reproduced, and the differences between library versions that were found on the way.

title: Reproducing models
section: The input models of the gravity controlled models
text:
The input models of the gravity controlled models
In July 2024, Sweco made the input models <authority>_2024_6_3 of the 11 gravity controlled water authorities with ribasim_lumping, at commit 65c7ef53 of #118, in four notebooks: apply manual changes to the HyDAMO data, lump the network into basins, and convert the result into a Ribasim model. This code is ported to ribasim_nl.lumping, and the DVC pipeline runs it:

pipeline/00a_process_hydamo.py applies the manual changes to the HyDAMO data of 7 water authorities. For Aa en Maas, De Dommel and Vallei en Veluwe, the processed HyDAMO data is source data.
pipeline/00b_lump_model.py lumps the HyDAMO network of 10 water authorities into their input model.
pipeline/noorderzijlvest/00_lump_model.py lumps the D-HYDRO model of Noorderzijlvest.

All node IDs and link IDs of the 11 input models are reproduced. In Limburg, whose input data differs from the data of the run in 2024, 4 nodes get another name. The basin areas are no longer reproduced, since the lumping now gives every area to a basin, see Moving fixes into the lumping.

title: Reproducing models
section: The input models of the level controlled models
text:
The input models of the level controlled models
HKV made the input models <authority>_boezemmodel_<version> of the 10 level controlled water authorities with peilbeheerst_model, in three steps: parse_crossings found the crossings of the hydro-objects with the boundaries of the peilgebieden in spring 2024, notebooks found the shortest paths through the boezems, and crossings_to_ribasim made the models on 4 December 2024, at commit 91b23140 of #244. Wetterskip Fryslân followed on 19 and 20 May 2025, at commit 50638080 of #331. This code is ported to ribasim_nl.crossings, together with the scripts that turned the data the water authorities delivered into the postprocessed data, see Level controlled.
All node IDs, link IDs and tables of the 10 input models are reproduced from the deliveries, but for one pump of Wetterskip Fryslân, see below. Some links to and from the boezems get another geometry, since they follow shortest paths, of which a few now take another route of the same length or have their vertices in another order, and some nodes and areas differ by less than a centimetre, see GEOS.

The postprocessed data
pipeline/<authority>/00_postprocess.py ports the preprocessing and postprocessing scripts of peilbeheerst_model, which are removed; see them at commit 1115d284. These scripts were not the version that made the data of 2024, which HKV ran locally: some no longer ran, others read other deliveries, or kept other rows. The ports reconstruct that version from the data of 2024, the deliveries on the cloud storage, and the notebooks of HKV in the git history, and reproduce the postprocessed data of 2024 exactly, but for:

the columns meta_name and meta_capaciteit, which nothing uses;
coordinates that differ by less than 1e-6 m, from reprojections with another PROJ and unions with another GEOS;
4 peilgebieden of Hollands Noorderkwartier, which HKV clipped by water board boundaries that are not on the cloud storage, and which differ by 1 to 4 m².

HKV corrected some of the delivered data by hand, such as gaps between the peilgebieden of Zuiderzeeland, and the KRW water bodies that became peilgebieden in Hollandse Delta. verwerkt/corrections.gpkg holds these corrections as edits of the delivered layers, which ribasim_nl.crossings.postprocess.derive_edits derived from the data of 2024, and which apply_edits applies in place, keeping the order of the rows. For Rijnland, it also holds the results of 2024 where GEOS 3.14 differs, see GEOS. The aggregation areas follow from the deliveries: copies of the peilgebieden, or polders, supply areas or drainage units that the peilgebieden are joined with. Only the 12 parts into which HKV split the boezem of Delfland are source data, verwerkt/aggregation_area.gpkg.
Other findings:

The delivered levels of Amstel, Gooi en Vecht and Rivierenland are float32 values such as -2.0999999 in the files themselves; HKV rounded them to centimetres, and so do the ports.
GDAL 3.13 splits a self-touching ring of a shapefile into an outer ring and a hole. Hollands Noorderkwartier reads its peilgebieden as stored, as GDAL 3.10 did.
ruff’s fix of 2024 changed comparisons of columns such as df.col == False into df.col is False, which is always false; the ports compare as before.



The node IDs
ribasim_nl.crossings.renumber numbers the nodes and links of the input models after those of 2024, verwerkt/boezemmodel_ids.gpkg, to which the feedback forms, the feedback scripts and the coupling refer. Basins match by the overlap of their areas, the other nodes by type and location, first those that connect the same Basins; nodes that are left match a node of the same type between the same Basins within 250 m. Unmatched nodes get IDs after the highest of 2024; links get the ID of the link between the same nodes. The feedback step numbers the links anew, in their order, so a link that is added or removed before it shifts the IDs of the links after it; the scripts that follow refer to links by their nodes.
With exactly the same postprocessed data, the input models have the same IDs, but the coordinate noise above swaps a few nodes at the same place: the renumbering changes 6 nodes of Amstel, Gooi en Vecht and 8 of Zuiderzeeland back. The crossings of Wetterskip Fryslân of May 2025 cannot be reproduced: the same code on the same data finds some stacked crossings in another order, with numpy 2.2 and GEOS 3.13, with or without AVX2 and AVX-512, and so does the port. After the renumbering, 3852 of its 3853 nodes keep their ID; 9 of them, crossings that moved along the boundary of their peilgebied, are 4 to 134 m from where they were, and one pump that the feedback form does not use is gone.
In Hollandse Delta, a hydro-object crosses the boundary between peilgebieden 94 and 95 almost in parallel, so the direction of the crossing depends on rounding: GEOS 3.12 found it from 95 to 94, GEOS 3.14 also from 94 to 95. pipeline/00c_parse_crossings.py excludes the second, and checks that it is found.

title: Reproducing models
text:
Process

Find the code and the data as they were. The git history has the code, and the cloud storage has the data with its modification dates. Compare the dates of the inputs with those of the outputs: an input that changed after the run cannot reproduce it.
Recreate the environment of the time, with the library versions of then, and run the original code on the current data. That gives the reference: differences between the reference and the original outputs come from the data, differences between the reference and the port come from the code.
Port the code, and compare its intermediate results with those of the original code, table by table and including the order of the rows, not only the final model. The order of rows is often the order of the IDs.
Where the order differs, emulate the old behaviour where the IDs follow from it, rather than sorting afterwards.
Run the downstream scripts on the original and on the reproduced model, and compare their results.

For the input models, the reference environment was a separate Pixi project with Python 3.12, pandas 2.1.4, numpy 1.26.4, geopandas 0.14.4, shapely 2.0.4 with GEOS 3.12.2, fiona 1.9.6, pyogrio 0.7 and networkx 3.3. The environment Sweco used is not known, but this one reproduces its IDs.
For the level controlled input models, three reference environments followed the lock files of then. The crossings: Python 3.12.2, numpy 1.26.4, pandas 2.2.1, geopandas 0.14.3, shapely 2.0.3 with GEOS 3.12.1, fiona 1.9.6, pyogrio 0.7.2 and networkx 3.3, without AVX-512, which NPY_DISABLE_CPU_FEATURES turns off. The input models of December 2024: Python 3.12.7, numpy 2.0.2, pandas 2.2.3, geopandas 1.0.1, shapely 2.0.6 with GEOS 3.13.0, ribasim 2024.11.0, pandera 0.20.4 and pydantic 2.9.2. That of May 2025: Python 3.13.3, numpy 2.2.5, pandas 2.2.3, shapely 2.1.0 with GEOS 3.13.1, networkx 3.4.2 and ribasim 2025.3.0.

title: Reproducing models
text:
GEOS
The results of geometric operations such as union, intersection, buffer(0) and make_valid differ between versions and builds of GEOS. Coordinates differ by about 1e-9 m, the results get other slivers and tiny holes, and adjacent parts of a union may or may not be merged. That cannot be emulated: GEOS 3.12.2 reproduces 858 of the 859 basin areas of De Dommel topologically, but only 190 of the 543 of Stichtse Rijnlanden.
The IDs of the level controlled models depend on it in one place: a crossing in Hollandse Delta that GEOS 3.14 finds in both directions, see above. Their shortest paths through the boezems depend on it as well: a few take another route of the same length, or merge their lines with the vertices in another order, which gives their links another geometry. And in Rijnland, 56 peilgebieden without crossings get another aggregation area in the column agg_area of the peilgebieden of the crossings, since GEOS 3.14 computes other overlaps with the aggregation areas; nothing uses it. Its postprocessing takes the praktijk peilgebieden off the vigerend ones, which leaves mostly slivers along their boundaries, and adds a margin of 1 m to the parts of its boezem. GEOS 3.14 makes other slivers and margins than GEOS 3.12 did, so verwerkt/corrections.gpkg holds those of 2024 where they differ, in the layers remnants and boezem.
The IDs of the gravity controlled models do not depend on it, but scripts that select geometries do. They now allow for these differences:

Model.select_basin_area, used by remove_basin_area and update_basin_area, takes geometries as equal if their boundaries are on average at most 1 mm apart. Without a basin area that equals a polygon, it selects the basin areas that together make it up, or else splits the polygon from the basin areas that cover it. So it works whether adjacent parts are merged or not. It skips slivers.
ribasim_nl.geometry.connected_parts splits a (Multi)Polygon in the parts connected to the part with a given point, and the other parts, instead of taking the parts by position.

A union with slivers can also go wrong, in GEOS 3.12 as well as 3.14: it can lose or add whole parts. In Hunze en Aas, a union of 25 pieces of a basin area lost 2.1 km², and the union of a basin area of 61 vertices with a sliver of 1e-9 m² gained 0.066 km². ribasim_nl.geometry.union_polygons checks that a union is not larger than the polygons together, and contains a point inside each polygon. If not, it takes the union again with a fixed precision of 1 mm, or without the slivers. The lumping and Model.dissolve_basin_area use it. That check does not catch a part lost within a large polygon, though. Overlays with a fixed precision (grid_size), on geometries made valid at that precision with shapely.set_precision, are robust. ribasim_nl.berging.supply_area_basin_ids overlays basin areas with supply areas that way, since a floating point overlay found no overlap for 3 basins of Drents Overijsselse Delta that lie entirely in a supply area.

title: Reproducing models
text:
Writing reproducible code

Sort with kind="stable", and with keys that decide the order of all rows that matter. The order of equal values in an unstable sort depends on the library version and the CPU.
Do not rely on the order of rows after a merge, a groupby or a spatial join; sort explicitly where the order sets IDs.
Refer to objects by a stable key, such as their code, rather than by row number. gpd.read_file(..., fid_as_index=True) makes a script depend on the order of the rows in the file, so keep that order when such a file is rewritten.
Select geometries with a tolerance, and do not rely on the order or number of the parts of geometries from geometric operations.
Do not let a result depend on whether geometries touch. Whether the end of a line on a boundary reaches into a polygon by 1e-9 m depends on coordinate noise. The profiles counted a hydro-object with its whole length in every basin it intersected, so noise of at most 1e-8 m changed 185 of the 215 Basin profiles of Zuiderzeeland, with bottoms up to 4.85 m apart, while its network hardly changed. ribasim_nl.profiles.path_finder.overlaps requires an overlap of 1 mm. Rounding the coordinates also removes the noise, but lines then still count in polygons they only touch, decided by the rounding.
Of the shortest paths of equal length, networkx takes the one it reaches first, which depends on the order in which the graph was built. Build graphs from geometries in an order that follows from them, as ribasim_nl.profiles.path_finder.canonical does.
Where the result of an overlay decides something, overlay with a fixed precision, on geometries made valid at that precision.
The DVC pipeline records the code, data and environment of every output, in git, dvc.lock and pixi.lock, so an output can always be reproduced.

title: Reproducing models
text:
Moving fixes into the lumping
The 01_fix_model.py scripts correct the input models afterwards. Now that the pipeline makes the input models, most of these fixes can move into the lumping or its inputs, or the lumping algorithm can change, so that the input models are right from the start. These have moved:

Lost basins. The lumping of 2024 left out the basins whose ID was taken by a split node, and those at a LevelBoundary without split node, while links still referred to them. The fix scripts added them again, and removed the duplicate links. ribasim_nl.lumping.model.number_lost_basins now does that, with the IDs the fix scripts gave them.
Basin areas. Every area of verwerkt/3_input/areas.gpkg goes to a basin, see ribasim_nl.lumping.network.assign_areas: the basin it drains to, or else the basin with whose areas it shares the longest border, preferably in its drainage area. Each basin gets one MultiPolygon, and gaps between them up to 5000 m² are filled. The fix scripts no longer fill holes from verwerkt/4_ribasim/areas.gpkg, which differed from it for 3 authorities. As their last step, they fill the holes that their own edits leave with Model.fill_basin_area_holes, by the same rules, which also checks that every Basin has a basin area. A Basin that a fix script adds gets its areas by their code, since the area that its node lies in can be far too small. Parts outside the model are excluded there, such as the Twentekanaal of the Rijkswaterstaat model in Vechtstromen.

These remain:

Edits of the lumping inputs. Splitting basin areas with lines, or removing and renaming them with model_edits.gpkg, can become edits of the split nodes, boundaries and areas that the lumping reads, which have stable codes. The tolerant Model.select_basin_area only bridges until then. The area split lines of Stichtse Rijnlanden, for instance, were drawn on the basin areas of 2024. Splitting areas.gpkg along them before the lumping gives 20 of the 28 basins that need them an area by drainage.
Node IDs. They follow from the order of the boundaries, split nodes and basins, so a new split node renumbers all basins after it. That breaks the references to node IDs in the remaining fix scripts, in model_edits.gpkg, and in pipeline/09_koppelen_modellen.py. Move the fixes of an authority together, and where references remain, refer to nodes by a stable key, such as their code.

title: Running on SLURM
text: The pipeline up to koppelen can be reproduced on an HPC cluster using two scripts:

title: Running on SLURM
text:
repro.sh: pipeline reproduction
Submits the DVC pipeline as individual SLURM jobs. Each authority gets one job that runs its stages in order, and SLURM --dependency=afterok ensures correct ordering.
./repro.sh
This submits jobs in these waves:

clean: removes the outputs of all stages that are run, like dvc repro does, and runs dvc pull --force for everything upstream of them; no manual pull is needed
rwzi and peilbeheer (shared dependencies)
22 parallel jobs: 11 from parameterized to dynamic, 10 from feedback to forcing, and 1 with hws_demand and hws_transient
samenvoegen → koppelen
commit: dvc commit, pixi run check and dvc push

It does not run the input-model stages (such as lumped and boezemmodel), whose outputs clean pulls, nor the frozen bathymetry, nor the stages after koppelen. To also run those, use pixi run repro-local.
The job IDs of samenvoegen, koppelen and commit are written to repro_jobs.txt when submitting, for use with run.sh.

title: Running on SLURM
text:
run.sh: isolated simulation runs
Copies a model to /p/ribasim-nl/runs/<name>/ and submits a SLURM job using the named Ribasim core configured in scripts/install_ribasim_core.py.
As an immediate preparation step, run.sh runs the archive-core Pixi task. This task depends on install-core, then archives bin/ribasim at /p/ribasim-nl/bin/<NAME>. Pixi skips the copy when the input directory and installer configuration are unchanged.
Named archives are immutable: archive-core does not replace an existing /p/ribasim-nl/bin/<NAME> directory. Change NAME when archiving a different core.
The submitted SLURM job runs this archived executable, not bin/ribasim in the repository. The repository and its installed core can therefore change while simulations are queued or running without changing the executable used by those simulations. The exact Ribasim version is written to each SLURM log before the model starts.
./run.sh <name> <model_dir> [--after=<jobid>] [key=value ...]
TOML overrides use dot notation for nested keys.

Examples
Run lhm_coupled after koppelen finishes:
./run.sh lhm_coupled data/Rijkswaterstaat/modellen/lhm_coupled \
  --after=$(grep koppelen repro_jobs.txt | cut -f2)
Run lhm_coupled with a shorter simulation period:
./run.sh lhm_coupled_1yr data/Rijkswaterstaat/modellen/lhm_coupled \
  --after=$(grep koppelen repro_jobs.txt | cut -f2) \
  endtime="2018-01-01 00:00:00"
Compare solver settings:
./run.sh lhm_coupled_tight data/Rijkswaterstaat/modellen/lhm_coupled \
  --after=$(grep koppelen repro_jobs.txt | cut -f2) \
  solver.abstol=1e-6

./run.sh lhm_coupled_qndf data/Rijkswaterstaat/modellen/lhm_coupled \
  --after=$(grep koppelen repro_jobs.txt | cut -f2) \
  solver.algorithm=QNDF solver.abstol=1e-5
All submissions are logged to /p/ribasim-nl/runs/jobs.txt. The job logs of repro.sh are gitignored.

title: Type checking
text: We use ty for static type checking. ty is configured in the [tool.ty] section of pyproject.toml.

title: Type checking
text:
Running ty
To check for type errors, run:
pixi run typecheck
The same task is run by the typecheck pre-commit hook.

title: Type checking
text:
Rule overrides
Rule-specific, per-file exceptions are configured with [[tool.ty.overrides]] entries. Default rules remain enabled everywhere else. Prefer fixing typing issues, and remove files or rules from these overrides when they are no longer needed. Do not add global rule suppressions.

Suppressing individual errors
For specific lines where the type checker is wrong, use a targeted ignore comment:
x = some_expression  # ty: ignore[error-code]
For lines that would exceed 120 characters with the comment appended, place the comment on the line above:
# ty: ignore[error-code]
x = some_very_long_expression_that_would_be_too_long_with_an_inline_comment

title: Ribasim-NL
text: Ribasim-NL builds the Dutch national water model LHM with Ribasim, a water resources model. It combines a model of the main water system of Rijkswaterstaat with the regional models of 21 water authorities, from their source data, into one model of about 20 000 Basins. A DVC pipeline in this repository makes every step reproducible, so a change to the data or the code gives a new model that can be compared with the previous one.

section: From source data to a nationwide model

  hkv["Level areas, structures<br>10 water authorities"] --> level["Level controlled<br>regional models"]

    meta_streefpeil=None,

    to_node_id,
    data,

Add a control_node to the network


to_node_id : int | list node_id or list of node_ids to connect control node to data: data for the control node
offset_node_id : int | None, optional User can explicitly specify a offset_node_id for a left-offset of the control-node. by default None node_geom : tuple | None, optional User can explicitly specify an Point for the control node. Alternative method to add links to the model.
model.link.add() sometimes raises AttributeError: Flagsobject has no attribute _allows_duplicate_labels when calling _concat(). Untill this can be solved we bypass by concating a non-pydantic-schemed GeoDataFrame to the link-table.

Model.apply_edits(edits_gpkg, actions, *, sort_by_order=False, drop_na=False)
Apply model edits stored in a GeoPackage, with a layer per edit method (action).

Get downstream node_id(s)

Get upstream basin-profile



Model.fill_basin_area_holes(areas_gpkg, excluded=None)
Give the parts of the areas of areas_gpkg that no basin area covers to a Basin, one basin area per Basin.
The uncovered part of an area goes to the Basin that covers most of that area, and an area that none covers to the Basin it shares the longest border with, preferably in the same drainage area, as in the lumping, see ribasim_nl.lumping.network.fill_holes. Model.run(**kwargs)
Run your Ribasim model



Model.select_basin_area(geometry, tolerance=0.001)
Select the basin areas that equal geometry, or else each of its polygons.
Geometries are taken as equal if their boundaries are on average at most tolerance m apart. That allows for the differences between the results of versions of GEOS, which can also merge or separate adjacent parts of an area. So without a basin area that equals a polygon, the basin areas that together make it up are selected, or else the polygon is split from the basin areas that cover it, as basin areas of the same nodes. Polygons on average narrower than tolerance are slivers, which differ between versions of GEOS, and are not selected.

)

NetworkValidator(model, tolerance=1)
Contains some methods for validating a Ribasim-model


model: Model Ribasim model tolerance: float (default=1) Tolerance to use for snapping. Should be in the units of the model.crs






Name
Description




link_duplicated
Check if the from_node_id and to_node_id in the link-table is duplicated


link_incorrect_connectivity
Check if the geometries of the from_node_id and to_node_id are on the start and end vertices of the link-geometry within tolerance (default=1m)


link_incorrect_from_node
Check if the from_node_type in link-table in matches the node_type of the corresponding node in the node-table


link_incorrect_to_node
Check if the to_node_type in link-table in matches the node_type of the corresponding node in the node-table


link_incorrect_type_connectivity
Check links that contain wrong connectivity


link_missing_nodes
Check if the from_node_id and to_node_id in the link-table are both as node-id in the node-table


node_duplicated

title: flow_paths
text:
flow_paths
Routes of flow links through Junctions, and changes to them that only change the layout.
A Junction only merges or splits flow, so the flow links from a node through Junctions up to the next non-Junction nodes form the route of that node. Ribasim replaces each pair of links into and out of a Junction by a direct link, see simplify_graph! in the Ribasim core. Moving or adding Junctions on a route therefore changes how links are drawn, not how water flows, as long as each node keeps exchanging water with the same non-Junction nodes.





Name
Description




Routes
The routes of the flow links of a model, as they are when the Routes are made.





flow_paths.Routes(model)
The routes of the flow links of a model, as they are when the Routes are made.





Name
Description




ends
The first non-Junction nodes downstream of a flow link, or upstream if upstream, through Junctions.


links_at
The flow links into node_id if upstream, else out of it.


next_node
The node a flow link comes from if upstream, else goes to.


paths
The route of node_id downstream, or upstream if upstream: the path from node_id to each of its links.





flow_paths.Routes.ends(link_id, upstream=False)
The first non-Junction nodes downstream of a flow link, or upstream if upstream, through Junctions.



flow_paths.Routes.links_at(node_id, upstream)
The flow links into node_id if upstream, else out of it.



flow_paths.Routes.next_node(link_id, upstream)
The node a flow link comes from if upstream, else goes to.



flow_paths.Routes.paths(node_id, upstream=False)
The route of node_id downstream, or upstream if upstream: the path from node_id to each of its links.
Only links whose own route in the other direction ends at node_id alone are part of it, so for a Basin these are the links that only carry water out of that Basin, or upstream, only into it.









Name
Description




attach_to_tree
Attach points to the tree of routes from start, each with a straight line from the nearest point of the tree.


branch_from_route
Let the link from basin_id into node_id branch off the route from basin_id towards towards_id.


geometry_along
The line from the start of a route path, see Routes.paths, to distance along its last link.


junction_tree
The Junctions that only pass flow out of basin_id, or into it if upstream, and the nodes they reach.


merge_inflows
Replace the flow links from basin_id to node_ids by a link to a new Junction, with straight links on.


merge_outflows
Connect node_ids with straight links to the first Junction downstream that all of their routes pass.


place_on_link
Move node_id onto the point of link_id nearest to it, with its link with basin_id along their route.


prune_junction
Remove a Junction without inflow or outflow, or merge the two links of a Junction that only passes flow on.


rebuild_junction_trees
Route the flow links of Basins along the waterways, with their Junctions where the routes split.


rebuild_junction_trees_along_top10nl
Rebuild the Junctions of Basins along the Top10NL water lines and a main route, see rebuild_junction_trees.


remove_flow_link
Remove a flow link, and prune the Junctions at its ends, see prune_junction.


simplified_links
The flow links between non-Junction nodes that Ribasim makes of the flow links, through Junctions.


split_distance
The distance along geometry of the point nearest to point, at least margin from its ends if possible.


split_link
Split a flow link at distance along it with a Junction: node_id moved there, or else a new one.


tree_links
The links of the tree of routes that all start at the same point, with a Junction where they split.





flow_paths.attach_to_tree(routes, start, points)
Attach points to the tree of routes from start, each with a straight line from the nearest point of the tree.
The points nearest to the tree are attached first, such that the others can branch off their lines. Where a line branches off a segment, a point is inserted in all routes along that segment, such that they share it.











Name
Type
Description
Default




routes
dict[int, list[Coord]]
per key, the coordinates of a route from start
required


start
Coord
the start of the routes, from which the first point is attached if there are no routes
required


points
dict[int, Coord]
per key, a point to attach
required














Name
Type
Description





dict[int, list[Coord]]
the routes, with a route to each point







flow_paths.branch_from_route(model, node_id, basin_id, towards_id, margin=1.0)
Let the link from basin_id into node_id branch off the route from basin_id towards towards_id.
The branch starts at a Junction at the point of that route nearest to node_id, or at the existing Junction if that point is within margin of one, and runs straight to node_id. Returns the node id of that Junction.



flow_paths.geometry_along(model, path, distance, upstream)
The line from the start of a route path, see Routes.paths, to distance along its last link.



flow_paths.junction_tree(routes, basin_id, upstream=False, fixed=())
The Junctions that only pass flow out of basin_id, or into it if upstream, and the nodes they reach.
Junctions in fixed, and Junctions that also pass flow of other nodes, are not part of the tree but reached by it.










Name
Type
Description





tuple[set[int], list[int], dict[int, int]]
the Junctions of the tree, the links between basin_id and them, and per node reached, its link







flow_paths.merge_inflows(model, basin_id, node_ids)
Replace the flow links from basin_id to node_ids by a link to a new Junction, with straight links on.
The Junction is at the centroid of node_ids, see place_on_link to move it. Returns its node id.



flow_paths.merge_outflows(model, node_ids)
Connect node_ids with straight links to the first Junction downstream that all of their routes pass.
The Junctions they passed before are pruned. Returns the node id of the Junction.



flow_paths.place_on_link(model, node_id, basin_id, link_id)
Move node_id onto the point of link_id nearest to it, with its link with basin_id along their route.
link_id is on the route of basin_id in either direction, see Routes.paths, and node_id has a single flow link with basin_id. Its other links move their ends along.



flow_paths.prune_junction(model, junction_id)
Remove a Junction without inflow or outflow, or merge the two links of a Junction that only passes flow on.
Neighboring Junctions are pruned in turn. A Junction with other links, such as observation links, is kept.



flow_paths.rebuild_junction_trees(model, basin_ids, waterways, tolerance=10.0)
Route the flow links of Basins along the waterways, with their Junctions where the routes split.
The Junctions of a Basin are removed if they only pass the flow out of, or into, that Basin, see junction_tree, except observed Junctions and RWZI Junctions. The links to the nodes they reach are routed from the Basin node along the shortest paths of one network, see ribasim_nl.network_snapping.route_basin_links, such that the routes out of and into a Basin share their common parts, and new Junctions are added where they split. Nodes far from the waterways branch off straight from the nearest point of these routes, see attach_to_tree, also over open water, where routes over the water surface would run in parallel. Each node keeps exchanging water with the same nodes, which is asserted, and the links to the nodes reached keep their link ids. Nodes are not moved and links are not offset, see ribasim_nl.layout.tidy_layout.

Type
Description
Default




model
Model
Ribasim model
required


basin_ids
typing.Iterable[int]
Basins to rebuild the Junctions of
required


waterways
gpd.GeoDataFrame
waterways with a boolean “main-route” column, see ribasim_nl.network_snapping.snap_to_network
required


tolerance
float
buffer around the basin area within which waterways are used, defaults to 10.0
10.0














Name
Type
Description





tuple[list[int], list[int]]
the ids of the links and of the Junctions that are new or changed







flow_paths.rebuild_junction_trees_along_top10nl(
    model,
    basin_ids,
    top10nl_path,
    main_route,
    tolerance=250.0,
)
Rebuild the Junctions of Basins along the Top10NL water lines and a main route, see rebuild_junction_trees.
This is used for the hws model and again after coupling, such that its Basins keep their routes. Its connector nodes are often outside the area of their Basin, so waterways up to tolerance around it are used.



flow_paths.remove_flow_link(model, link_id)
Remove a flow link, and prune the Junctions at its ends, see prune_junction.



flow_paths.simplified_links(model)
The flow links between non-Junction nodes that Ribasim makes of the flow links, through Junctions.



flow_paths.split_distance(geometry, point, margin=1.0)
The distance along geometry of the point nearest to point, at least margin from its ends if possible.



flow_paths.split_link(model, link_id, distance, node_id=None)
Split a flow link at distance along it with a Junction: node_id moved there, or else a new one.
Returns the node id of the Junction. Other links of an existing node_id move their ends along.



flow_paths.tree_links(routes)
The links of the tree of routes that all start at the same point, with a Junction where they split.
The last segment of each route is its own, so a route that is part of another one still ends in a branch.











Name
Type
Description
Default




routes
dict[int, list[Coord]]
per key, the coordinates of a route
required














Name
Type
Description





list[tuple[_TreeNode, _TreeNode, list[Coord]]]
the links from the start “root” to Junctions (“junction”, number), and to the end (“end”, key) of each route, with their coordinates, such that the link into a Junction comes before the links out of it

title: goodness_of_fit
text:
goodness_of_fit
How well the simulated values of a model run fit the measurements of its Observation nodes.
observed_and_simulated pairs the measured values of each Observation node with the simulated values of the node it observes, and compare summarizes how well they fit. ribasim_nl.result_validation checks the fit of a run of the coupled LHM model, and ribasim_nl.webmap exports it for the model viewer.





Name
Description




ObservedSeries
The measured values of a variable of an Observation node, and the simulated values of the node it observes.





goodness_of_fit.ObservedSeries(
    node_id,
    name,
    variable,
    observed_node_id,
    observed,
    simulated,
)
The measured values of a variable of an Observation node, and the simulated values of the node it observes.







Name
Description




compare
Goodness of fit of a simulated to an observed time series, on the times at which both have a value.


compare_observations
Compare each Observation node with the simulated values of the node it observes, see compare.


observed_and_simulated
The measured and simulated values of each observed variable of each Observation node, by node ID and variable.


read_table
Read columns of a table of a Ribasim database, which is empty if the table does not exist.





goodness_of_fit.compare(observed, simulated)
Goodness of fit of a simulated to an observed time series, on the times at which both have a value.
The Nash-Sutcliffe (NSE) and Kling-Gupta efficiencies (KGE) are NaN if there are fewer than MIN_COMPARED_DAYS values, or if the observations are constant. The bias is relative to the mean absolute observation.



goodness_of_fit.compare_observations(database, results_dir)
Compare each Observation node with the simulated values of the node it observes, see compare.










Name
Type
Description





pd.DataFrame
a table by the node ID of the Observation, with its name, the observed node and the result of compare







goodness_of_fit.observed_and_simulated(database, results_dir)
The measured and simulated values of each observed variable of each Observation node, by node ID and variable.
Like in the model viewer, the simulated flow rate of a node is its total outflow, which for a Junction is the flow through it, and other variables are those of an observed Basin. Observation nodes without a link to the node they observe are left out.



goodness_of_fit.read_table(con, table, columns)
Read columns of a table of a Ribasim database, which is empty if the table does not exist.

text:
junctionify
junctionify(model)
Add Junction nodes in a model inplace where flow links share common geometry.
Useful for model visualization and debugging, as otherwise there will be many overlapping line segments that are hard to distinguish.
Assumes that all flow link geometries between node a and b start with point a and end with point b.

title: network_snapping
text:
network_snapping
Route link geometries of a Ribasim-scheme along the network of hydro-objects.
Nodes are never moved: connector nodes stay at the location of the structure they represent, and Basin nodes stay where they are. Only the geometries of the flow links between a Basin and a connector node are changed. Such a link is drawn as a straight line from the connector node to the nearest hydro-object within the basin area, followed by the shortest route along the hydro-objects to the point nearest to the Basin node, and a straight line to the Basin node. Links that share a route can afterwards be merged with ribasim_nl.junctions.junctionify.
This relies on the network of hydro-objects written by the network-based profile-generation: src/ribasim_nl/ribasim_nl/profiles/*.py.

Route the links between a Basin node and its connector nodes along the hydro-objects in the basin.
The hydro-objects are connected by the culverts, and dangling ends are connected to other parts of the network if the gap is small or crossed over water, see _BasinNetwork.bridge_gaps. Then only the longest connected part of the network is used. The Basin node is attached to its nearest main route hydro-object in this part (if any), and each connector node to its nearest hydro-object within max_attach_distance. Connector nodes farther away are attached over the water within area instead, crossing at most max_land of land, see _WaterRaster. All routes follow the shortest paths from the Basin node, such that routes share their common parts exactly.
If basin_area is given and contains the attachment point of the Basin node, and at least min_routed_fraction of the links can be routed from there, the Basin node is moved there. A route is not used if it is not less than max_straight_line_ratio times the straight line, as in ribasim_nl.link_geometries.fix_link_geometries.

title: peilbeheer
text:
peilbeheer
The level management (peilbeheer) of the peilgebieden of the water boards, in summer and winter.
The water boards deliver their peilgebieden in their own formats. read_peilbeheer reads them with the attribute mappings of SOURCES, see https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/893, into one table with per peilgebied the type of level management, the target level (streefpeil) and its lower and upper bound (ondergrens and bovengrens) in summer and winter, and the dates of the transitions between them. Where a dataset does not give these, they follow from the rules of complete_peilbeheer:

Without a target level, the target level is the mean of the bounds.
A season without a target level gets the levels of the other season, as for a fixed level.
Without a bound, or with a bound that does not lie within MAX_BOUND_DISTANCE beyond the target level, the bound is DEFAULT_BOUND from the target level, which is the band of the DiscreteControl thresholds of the model.
The transition from the winter to the summer level is from 1 to 10 April, and back from 1 to 10 October. Datasets with only the date at which the level changes start a transition of TRANSITION_DAYS days on that date. The models change their levels at once, at the begin of a transition, see ribasim_nl.seasonal_levels.

Levels of 99 m from NAP or more are unknown values, and so are levels of 0 in datasets that use 0 for unknown values, see valid_levels. Peilgebieden of which the summer and winter level differ more than MAX_SEASONAL_DIFFERENCE are data errors, and skipped. Most peilgebieden are areas, but they can also be points, such as weirs with their target levels.

Steps shared by the regional models of all water authorities, vrij afwaterend and peilbeheerst alike.

    model,
